   385→func runRewindToInternal(ctx context.Context, commitID string, logsOnly bool, reset bool) error {
   386→	start := GetStrategy(ctx)
   387→
   388→	// Check for uncommitted changes (skip for reset which handles this itself)
   389→	if !reset {
   390→		canRewind, changeMsg, err := start.CanRewind(ctx)
   391→		if err != nil {
   392→			return fmt.Errorf("failed to check for uncommitted changes: %w", err)
   393→		}
   394→		if !canRewind {
   395→			return fmt.Errorf("%s", changeMsg)
   396→		}
   397→	}
   398→
   399→	// Get rewind points
   400→	points, err := start.GetRewindPoints(ctx, 20)
   401→	if err != nil {
   402→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to find rewind points: %w", err)
   403→	}
   404→
   405→	// Find the matching point (support both full and short commit IDs)
   406→	var selectedPoint *strategy.RewindPoint
   407→	for _, p := range points {
   408→		if p.ID == commitID || (len(commitID) >= 7 && len(p.ID) >= 7 && strings.HasPrefix(p.ID, commitID)) {
   409→			pointCopy := p
   410→			selectedPoint = &pointCopy
   411→			break
   412→		}
   413→	}
   414→
   415→	if selectedPoint == nil {
   416→		return fmt.Errorf("rewind point not found: %s", commitID)
   417→	}
   418→
   419→	// Handle reset mode (for logs-only points)
   420→	if reset {
   421→		return handleLogsOnlyResetNonInteractive(ctx, start, *selectedPoint)
   422→	}
   423→
   424→	// Handle logs-only restoration:
   425→	// 1. For logs-only points, always use logs-only restoration
   426→	// 2. If --logs-only flag is set, use logs-only restoration even for checkpoint points
   427→	if selectedPoint.IsLogsOnly || logsOnly {
   428→		return handleLogsOnlyRewindNonInteractive(ctx, start, *selectedPoint)
   429→	}
   430→
   431→	// Preview rewind to show warnings about files that will be deleted
   432→	preview, previewErr := start.PreviewRewind(ctx, *selectedPoint)
   433→	if previewErr == nil && preview != nil && len(preview.FilesToDelete) > 0 {
   434→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "\nWarning: The following untracked files will be DELETED:\n")
   435→		for _, f := range preview.FilesToDelete {
   436→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "  - %s\n", f)
   437→		}
   438→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "\n")
   439→	}
   440→
   441→	// Resolve agent once for use throughout
   442→	agent, err := getAgent(selectedPoint.Agent)
   443→	if err != nil {
   444→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get agent: %w", err)
   445→	}
   446→
   447→	// Initialize logging context with agent from checkpoint
   448→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "rewind")
   449→	logCtx = logging.WithAgent(logCtx, agent.Name())
   450→
   451→	logging.Debug(logCtx, "rewind started",
   452→		slog.String("checkpoint_id", selectedPoint.ID),
   453→		slog.String("session_id", selectedPoint.SessionID),
   454→		slog.Bool("is_task_checkpoint", selectedPoint.IsTaskCheckpoint),
   455→	)
   456→
   457→	// Perform the rewind
   458→	if err := start.Rewind(ctx, *selectedPoint); err != nil {
   459→		logging.Error(logCtx, "rewind failed",
   460→			slog.String("checkpoint_id", selectedPoint.ID),
   461→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   462→		)
   463→		return err //nolint:wrapcheck // already present in codebase
   464→	}
   465→
   466→	logging.Debug(logCtx, "rewind completed",
   467→		slog.String("checkpoint_id", selectedPoint.ID),
   468→	)
   469→
   470→	// Handle transcript restoration
   471→	var sessionID string
   472→	var transcriptFile string
   473→
   474→	if selectedPoint.IsTaskCheckpoint {
   475→		checkpoint, err := start.GetTaskCheckpoint(ctx, *selectedPoint)
   476→		if err != nil {
   477→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to read task checkpoint: %v\n", err)
   478→			return nil
   479→		}
   480→
   481→		sessionID = checkpoint.SessionID
   482→
   483→		if checkpoint.CheckpointUUID != "" {
   484→			// Use strategy-based transcript restoration for task checkpoints
   485→			if err := restoreTaskCheckpointTranscript(ctx, start, *selectedPoint, sessionID, checkpoint.CheckpointUUID, agent); err != nil {
   486→				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to restore truncated session transcript: %v\n", err)
   487→			} else {
   488→				fmt.Printf("Rewound to task checkpoint. %s\n", agent.FormatResumeCommand(sessionID))
   489→			}
   490→			return nil
   491→		}
   492→	} else {
   493→		// Prefer SessionID from trailer over path-based extraction
   494→		sessionID = selectedPoint.SessionID
   495→		if sessionID == "" {
   496→			sessionID = filepath.Base(selectedPoint.MetadataDir)
   497→		}
   498→		transcriptFile = filepath.Join(selectedPoint.MetadataDir, paths.TranscriptFileNameLegacy)
   499→	}
   500→
   501→	// Try to restore transcript using the appropriate method:
   502→	// 1. Checkpoint storage (committed checkpoints with valid checkpoint ID)
   503→	// 2. Shadow branch (uncommitted checkpoints with commit hash)
   504→	// 3. Local file (active sessions)
   505→	var restored bool
   506→	if !selectedPoint.CheckpointID.IsEmpty() {
   507→		// Try checkpoint storage first for committed checkpoints
   508→		if returnedSessionID, err := restoreSessionTranscriptFromStrategy(ctx, selectedPoint.CheckpointID, sessionID, agent); err == nil {
   509→			sessionID = returnedSessionID
   510→			restored = true
   511→		}
   512→	}
   513→
   514→	if !restored && selectedPoint.MetadataDir != "" && len(selectedPoint.ID) == 40 {
   515→		// Try shadow branch for uncommitted checkpoints (ID is a 40-char commit hash)
   516→		if returnedSessionID, err := restoreSessionTranscriptFromShadow(ctx, selectedPoint.ID, selectedPoint.MetadataDir, sessionID, agent); err == nil {
   517→			sessionID = returnedSessionID
   518→			restored = true
   519→		}
   520→	}
   521→
   522→	if !restored {
   523→		// Fall back to local file
   524→		if err := restoreSessionTranscript(ctx, transcriptFile, sessionID, agent); err != nil {
   525→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to restore session transcript: %v\n", err)
   526→		}
   527→	}
   528→
   529→	fmt.Printf("Rewound to %s. %s\n", selectedPoint.ID[:7], agent.FormatResumeCommand(sessionID))
   530→	return nil
   531→}

   616→	)
   617→
   618→	shortID := point.ID
   619→	if len(shortID) > 7 {

   671→	if returnedSessionID != "" {

   694→// restoreSessionTranscriptFromShadow restores a session transcript from a shadow branch commit.
   695→// This is used for uncommitted checkpoints where the transcript is stored in the shadow branch tree.
   696→func restoreSessionTranscriptFromShadow(ctx context.Context, commitHash, metadataDir, sessionID string, agent agentpkg.Agent) (string, error) {
   697→	// Open repository
   698→	repo, err := git.PlainOpenWithOptions(".", &git.PlainOpenOptions{DetectDotGit: true})
   699→	if err != nil {
   700→		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to open repository: %w", err)
   701→	}
   702→
   703→	// Parse commit hash
   704→	hash := plumbing.NewHash(commitHash)
   705→	if hash.IsZero() {
   706→		return "", fmt.Errorf("invalid commit hash: %s", commitHash)
   707→	}
   708→
   709→	// Get transcript from shadow branch commit tree
   710→	store := checkpoint.NewGitStore(repo)
   711→	content, err := store.GetTranscriptFromCommit(ctx, hash, metadataDir, agent.Type())
   712→	if err != nil {
   713→		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to get transcript from shadow branch: %w", err)
   714→	}
   715→
   716→	sessionFile, err := resolveTranscriptPath(ctx, sessionID, agent)
   717→	if err != nil {
   718→		return "", err
   719→	}
   720→	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(sessionFile), 0o750); err != nil {
   721→		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to create agent session directory: %w", err)
   722→	}
   723→	agentSession := &agentpkg.AgentSession{
   724→		SessionID:  sessionID,
   725→		AgentName:  agent.Name(),
   726→		SessionRef: sessionFile,
   727→		NativeData: content,
   728→	}
   729→	if err := agent.WriteSession(ctx, agentSession); err != nil {
   730→		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to write session: %w", err)
   731→	}
   732→	return sessionID, nil
   733→}

   735→// restoreTaskCheckpointTranscript restores a truncated transcript for a task checkpoint.
   736→// Uses GetTaskCheckpointTranscript to fetch the transcript from the strategy.
   737→//
   738→// NOTE: The transcript parsing/truncation/writing pipeline (transcript.ParseFromBytes,
   739→// TruncateTranscriptAtUUID, writeTranscript) assumes Claude's JSONL format.
   740→// This is acceptable because task checkpoints are currently only created by Claude Code's
   741→// PostToolUse hook. If other agents gain sub-agent support, this will need a
   742→// format-aware refactor (agent-specific parsing, truncation, and serialization).
   743→func restoreTaskCheckpointTranscript(ctx context.Context, strat *strategy.ManualCommitStrategy, point strategy.RewindPoint, sessionID, checkpointUUID string, agent agentpkg.Agent) error {
   744→	// Get transcript content from strategy
   745→	content, err := strat.GetTaskCheckpointTranscript(ctx, point)
   746→	if err != nil {
   747→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get task checkpoint transcript: %w", err)
   748→	}
   749→
   750→	// Parse the transcript
   751→	parsed, err := transcript.ParseFromBytes(content)
   752→	if err != nil {
   753→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to parse transcript: %w", err)
   754→	}
   755→
   756→	// Truncate at checkpoint UUID
   757→	truncated := TruncateTranscriptAtUUID(parsed, checkpointUUID)
   758→
   759→	sessionFile, err := resolveTranscriptPath(ctx, sessionID, agent)
   760→	if err != nil {
   761→		return err
   762→	}
   763→
   764→	// Ensure parent directory exists
   765→	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(sessionFile), 0o750); err != nil {
   766→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to create agent session directory: %w", err)
   767→	}
   768→
   769→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Writing truncated transcript to: %s\n", sessionFile)
   770→
   771→	if err := writeTranscript(sessionFile, truncated); err != nil {
   772→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to write truncated transcript: %w", err)
   773→	}
   774→
   775→	return nil
   776→}

   922→	if agentErr != nil {
   923→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get agent: %w", agentErr)
   924→	}
   925→
   926→	// Initialize logging context with agent from checkpoint
   927→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "rewind")
   928→	logCtx = logging.WithAgent(logCtx, agent.Name())
   929→
   930→	logging.Debug(logCtx, "logs-only reset (interactive) started",
   931→		slog.String("checkpoint_id", point.ID),
   932→		slog.String("session_id", point.SessionID),
   933→	)
   934→
   935→	sessions, restoreErr := start.RestoreLogsOnly(ctx, point, true) // force=true for explicit rewind
   936→	if restoreErr != nil {
   937→		logging.Error(logCtx, "logs-only reset failed during log restoration",
   938→			slog.String("checkpoint_id", point.ID),
   939→			slog.String("error", restoreErr.Error()),
   940→		)
   941→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to restore logs: %w", restoreErr)
   942→	}
   943→
   944→	// Get current HEAD before reset (for recovery message)
   945→	currentHead, err := getCurrentHeadHash(ctx)
   946→	if err != nil {
   947→		// Non-fatal - just won't show recovery message
   948→		currentHead = ""
   949→	}
   950→
   951→	// Get detailed uncommitted changes warning from strategy
   952→	var uncommittedWarning string
   953→	if _, warn, err := start.CanRewind(ctx); err == nil {
   954→		uncommittedWarning = warn
   955→	}
   956→
   957→	// Check for safety issues
   958→	warnings, err := checkResetSafety(ctx, point.ID, uncommittedWarning)
   959→	if err != nil {
   960→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to check reset safety: %w", err)
   961→	}
   962→
   963→	// Build confirmation message based on warnings
   964→	var confirmTitle, confirmDesc string
   965→	if len(warnings) > 0 {
   966→		confirmTitle = "⚠️  Reset branch with warnings?"
   967→		confirmDesc = "WARNING - the following issues were detected:\n" +
   968→			strings.Join(warnings, "\n") +
   969→			"\n\nThis will move your branch to " + shortID + " and DISCARD commits after it!"
   970→	} else {
   971→		confirmTitle = "Reset branch to " + shortID + "?"
   972→		confirmDesc = "This will move your branch pointer to this commit.\nCommits after this point will be orphaned (but recoverable via reflog)."
   973→	}
   974→
   975→	var confirm bool
   976→	confirmForm := NewAccessibleForm(
   977→		huh.NewGroup(
   978→			huh.NewConfirm().
   979→				Title(confirmTitle).
   980→				Description(confirmDesc).
   981→				Value(&confirm),
   982→		),
   983→	)
   984→
   985→	if err := confirmForm.Run(); err != nil {
   986→		return fmt.Errorf("confirmation cancelled: %w", err)
   987→	}
   988→
   989→	if !confirm {
   990→		fmt.Println("Reset cancelled. Session logs were still restored.")
   991→		printMultiSessionResumeCommands(sessions)
   992→		return nil
   993→	}
   994→
   995→	// Perform git reset --hard
   996→	if err := performGitResetHard(ctx, point.ID); err != nil {
   997→		logging.Error(logCtx, "logs-only reset failed during git reset",
   998→			slog.String("checkpoint_id", point.ID),
   999→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
  1000→		)
  1001→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to reset branch: %w", err)
  1002→	}
  1003→
  1004→	logging.Debug(logCtx, "logs-only reset (interactive) completed",
  1005→		slog.String("checkpoint_id", point.ID),
  1006→	)
  1007→
  1008→	fmt.Printf("Reset branch to %s.\n", shortID)
  1009→	printMultiSessionResumeCommands(sessions)
  1010→
  1011→	// Show recovery instructions
  1012→	if currentHead != "" && currentHead != point.ID {
  1013→		currentShort := currentHead
  1014→		if len(currentShort) > 7 {
  1015→			currentShort = currentShort[:7]
  1016→		}
  1017→		fmt.Printf("\nTo undo this reset: git reset --hard %s\n", currentShort)
  1018→	}
  1019→
  1020→	return nil
  1021→}

  1023→// getCurrentHeadHash returns the current HEAD commit hash.
  1024→func getCurrentHeadHash(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
  1025→	repo, err := openRepository(ctx)
  1026→	if err != nil {
  1027→		return "", err
  1028→	}
  1029→
  1030→	head, err := repo.Head()
  1031→	if err != nil {
  1032→		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to get HEAD: %w", err)
  1033→	}
  1034→
  1035→	return head.Hash().String(), nil
  1036→}

  1038→// checkResetSafety checks for potential issues before a git reset --hard.
  1039→// Returns a list of warning messages (empty if safe to proceed without warnings).
  1040→// If uncommittedChangesWarning is provided, it will be used instead of a generic warning.
  1041→func checkResetSafety(ctx context.Context, targetCommitHash string, uncommittedChangesWarning string) ([]string, error) {
  1042→	var warnings []string
  1043→
  1044→	repo, err := openRepository(ctx)
  1045→	if err != nil {
  1046→		return nil, err
  1047→	}
  1048→
  1049→	// Check for uncommitted changes
  1050→	if uncommittedChangesWarning != "" {
  1051→		// Use the detailed warning from strategy's CanRewind()
  1052→		warnings = append(warnings, uncommittedChangesWarning)
  1053→	} else {
  1054→		// Fall back to generic check
  1055→		worktree, err := repo.Worktree()
  1056→		if err != nil {
  1057→			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get worktree: %w", err)
  1058→		}
  1059→
  1060→		status, err := worktree.Status()
  1061→		if err != nil {
  1062→			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get status: %w", err)
  1063→		}
  1064→
  1065→		if !status.IsClean() {
  1066→			warnings = append(warnings, "• You have uncommitted changes that will be LOST")
  1067→		}
  1068→	}
  1069→
  1070→	// Check if current HEAD is ahead of target (we'd be discarding commits)
  1071→	head, err := repo.Head()
  1072→	if err != nil {
  1073→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get HEAD: %w", err)
  1074→	}
  1075→
  1076→	targetHash := plumbing.NewHash(targetCommitHash)
  1077→
  1078→	// Count commits between target and HEAD
  1079→	commitsAhead, err := countCommitsBetween(repo, targetHash, head.Hash())
  1080→	if err != nil {
  1081→		// Non-fatal - just can't show commit count
  1082→		commitsAhead = -1
  1083→	}
  1084→
  1085→	if commitsAhead > 0 {
  1086→		warnings = append(warnings, fmt.Sprintf("• %d commit(s) after this point will be orphaned", commitsAhead))
  1087→	}
  1088→
  1089→	return warnings, nil
  1090→}

  1092→// countCommitsBetween counts commits between ancestor and descendant.
  1093→// Returns 0 if ancestor == descendant, -1 on error.
  1094→func countCommitsBetween(repo *git.Repository, ancestor, descendant plumbing.Hash) (int, error) {
  1095→	if ancestor == descendant {
  1096→		return 0, nil
  1097→	}
  1098→
  1099→	// Walk from descendant back to ancestor
  1100→	count := 0
  1101→	current := descendant
  1102→
  1103→	for count < strategy.MaxCommitTraversalDepth { // Safety limit
  1104→		if current == ancestor {
  1105→			return count, nil
  1106→		}
  1107→
  1108→		commit, err := repo.CommitObject(current)
  1109→		if err != nil {
  1110→			return -1, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit: %w", err)
  1111→		}
  1112→
  1113→		if commit.NumParents() == 0 {
  1114→			// Reached root without finding ancestor - ancestor not in history
  1115→			return -1, nil
  1116→		}
  1117→
  1118→		count++
  1119→		current = commit.ParentHashes[0] // Follow first parent
  1120→	}
  1121→
  1122→	return -1, nil
  1123→}

  1125→// performGitResetHard performs a git reset --hard to the specified commit.
  1126→// Uses the git CLI instead of go-git because go-git's HardReset incorrectly
  1127→// deletes untracked directories (like .entire/) even when they're in .gitignore.
  1128→func performGitResetHard(ctx context.Context, commitHash string) error {
  1129→	if strings.HasPrefix(commitHash, "-") {
  1130→		return fmt.Errorf("reset failed: invalid commit hash %q", commitHash)
  1131→	}
  1132→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "reset", "--hard", commitHash)
  1133→	if output, err := cmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
  1134→		return fmt.Errorf("reset failed: %s: %w", strings.TrimSpace(string(output)), err)
  1135→	}
  1136→	return nil
  1137→}

  1139→// sanitizeForTerminal removes or replaces characters that cause rendering issues
  1140→// in terminal UI components. This includes emojis with skin-tone modifiers and
  1141→// other multi-codepoint characters that confuse width calculations.
  1142→func sanitizeForTerminal(s string) string {
  1143→	var result strings.Builder
  1144→	result.Grow(len(s))
  1145→
  1146→	for _, r := range s {
  1147→		// Skip emoji skin tone modifiers (U+1F3FB to U+1F3FF)
  1148→		if r >= 0x1F3FB && r <= 0x1F3FF {
  1149→			continue
  1150→		}
  1151→		// Skip zero-width joiners used in emoji sequences
  1152→		if r == 0x200D {
  1153→			continue
  1154→		}
  1155→		// Skip variation selectors (U+FE00 to U+FE0F)
  1156→		if r >= 0xFE00 && r <= 0xFE0F {
  1157→			continue
  1158→		}
  1159→		// Keep printable characters and common whitespace
  1160→		if unicode.IsPrint(r) || r == '\t' || r == '\n' {
  1161→			result.WriteRune(r)
  1162→		}
  1163→	}
  1164→
  1165→	return result.String()
  1166→}

  1168→// printMultiSessionResumeCommands prints resume commands for restored sessions.
  1169→// Each session may have a different agent, so per-session agent resolution is used.
  1170→func printMultiSessionResumeCommands(sessions []strategy.RestoredSession) {
  1171→	if len(sessions) == 0 {
  1172→		return
  1173→	}
  1174→
  1175→	if len(sessions) > 1 {
  1176→		fmt.Printf("\nRestored %d sessions. Resume with:\n", len(sessions))
  1177→	}
  1178→
  1179→	for i, sess := range sessions {
  1180→		ag, err := strategy.ResolveAgentForRewind(sess.Agent)
  1181→		if err != nil {
  1182→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "  Warning: could not resolve agent %q for session %s, skipping\n", sess.Agent, sess.SessionID)
  1183→			continue
  1184→		}
  1185→
  1186→		cmd := ag.FormatResumeCommand(sess.SessionID)
  1187→
  1188→		if len(sessions) > 1 {
  1189→			// Add "(most recent)" label to the last session
  1190→			if i == len(sessions)-1 {
  1191→				if sess.Prompt != "" {
  1192→					fmt.Printf("  %s  # %s (most recent)\n", cmd, sess.Prompt)
  1193→				} else {
  1194→					fmt.Printf("  %s  # (most recent)\n", cmd)
  1195→				}
  1196→			} else {
  1197→				if sess.Prompt != "" {
  1198→					fmt.Printf("  %s  # %s\n", cmd, sess.Prompt)
  1199→				} else {
  1200→					fmt.Printf("  %s\n", cmd)
  1201→				}
  1202→			}
  1203→		} else {
  1204→			if sess.Prompt != "" {
  1205→				fmt.Printf("%s  # %s\n", cmd, sess.Prompt)
  1206→			} else {
  1207→				fmt.Printf("%s\n", cmd)
  1208→			}
  1209→		}
  1210→	}
  1211→}

   187→// NormalizeAfterLoad applies backward-compatible migrations to state loaded from disk.
   188→// Call this after deserializing a State from JSON.
   189→func (s *State) NormalizeAfterLoad(ctx context.Context) {
   190→	// Normalize legacy phase values. "active_committed" was removed with the
   191→	// 1:1 checkpoint model in favor of the state machine handling commits
   192→	// during ACTIVE phase with immediate condensation.
   193→	if s.Phase == "active_committed" {
   194→		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "session")
   195→		logging.Info(logCtx, "migrating legacy active_committed phase to active",
   196→			slog.String("session_id", s.SessionID),
   197→		)
   198→		s.Phase = PhaseActive
   199→	}
   200→	// Also normalize via PhaseFromString to handle any other legacy/unknown values.
   201→	s.Phase = PhaseFromString(string(s.Phase))
   202→
   203→	// Migrate transcript fields: CheckpointTranscriptStart replaces both
   204→	// CondensedTranscriptLines and TranscriptLinesAtStart from older state files.
   205→	if s.CheckpointTranscriptStart == 0 {
   206→		if s.CondensedTranscriptLines > 0 {
   207→			s.CheckpointTranscriptStart = s.CondensedTranscriptLines
   208→		} else if s.TranscriptLinesAtStart > 0 {
   209→			s.CheckpointTranscriptStart = s.TranscriptLinesAtStart
   210→		}
   211→	}
   212→	// Clear deprecated fields so they aren't re-persisted.
   213→	// Note: this is a one-way migration. If the state is re-saved, older CLI versions
   214→	// will see 0 for these fields and fall back to scoping from the transcript start.
   215→	// This is acceptable since CLI upgrades are monotonic and the worst case is
   216→	// redundant transcript content in a condensation, not data loss.
   217→	s.CondensedTranscriptLines = 0
   218→	s.TranscriptLinesAtStart = 0
   219→
   220→	// Backfill AttributionBaseCommit for sessions created before this field existed.
   221→	// Without this, a mid-turn commit would migrate BaseCommit and the fallback in
   222→	// calculateSessionAttributions would use the migrated value, producing zero attribution.
   223→	if s.AttributionBaseCommit == "" && s.BaseCommit != "" {
   224→		s.AttributionBaseCommit = s.BaseCommit
   225→	}
   226→}

   311→
   312→	if err := os.MkdirAll(s.stateDir, 0o750); err != nil {
   313→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to create session state directory: %w", err)
   314→	}
   315→
   316→	data, err := jsonutil.MarshalIndentWithNewline(state, "", "  ")
   317→	if err != nil {
   318→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal session state: %w", err)
   319→	}
   320→
   321→	stateFile := s.stateFilePath(state.SessionID)
   322→
   323→	// Atomic write: write to temp file, then rename
   324→	tmpFile := stateFile + ".tmp"
   325→	if err := os.WriteFile(tmpFile, data, 0o600); err != nil {
   326→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to write session state: %w", err)
   327→	}
   328→	if err := os.Rename(tmpFile, stateFile); err != nil {
   329→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to rename session state file: %w", err)
   330→	}
   331→	return nil
   332→}

   334→// Clear removes the session state file for the given session ID.
   335→func (s *StateStore) Clear(ctx context.Context, sessionID string) error {
   336→	_ = ctx // Reserved for future use
   337→
   338→	// Validate session ID to prevent path traversal
   339→	if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(sessionID); err != nil {
   340→		return fmt.Errorf("invalid session ID: %w", err)
   341→	}
   342→
   343→	stateFile := s.stateFilePath(sessionID)
   344→
   345→	if err := os.Remove(stateFile); err != nil {
   346→		if os.IsNotExist(err) {
   347→			return nil // Already gone, not an error
   348→		}
   349→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to remove session state file: %w", err)
   350→	}
   351→	return nil
   352→}
   353→
   354→// RemoveAll removes the entire session state directory.
   355→// This is used during uninstall to completely remove all session state.
   356→func (s *StateStore) RemoveAll() error {
   357→	if err := os.RemoveAll(s.stateDir); err != nil {
   358→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to remove session state directory: %w", err)
   359→	}
   360→	return nil
   361→}
   362→
   363→// List returns all session states.
   364→func (s *StateStore) List(ctx context.Context) ([]*State, error) {
   365→	entries, err := os.ReadDir(s.stateDir)
   366→	if os.IsNotExist(err) {
   367→		return nil, nil
   368→	}
   369→	if err != nil {
   370→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read session state directory: %w", err)
   371→	}
   372→
   373→	var states []*State
   374→	for _, entry := range entries {
   375→		if entry.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(entry.Name(), ".json") {
   376→			continue
   377→		}
   378→		if strings.HasSuffix(entry.Name(), ".tmp") {
   379→			continue // Skip temp files
   380→		}
   381→
   382→		sessionID := strings.TrimSuffix(entry.Name(), ".json")
   383→		state, err := s.Load(ctx, sessionID)
   384→		if err != nil {
   385→			continue // Skip corrupted state files
   386→		}
   387→		if state == nil {
   388→			continue // Not found or stale (Load handles cleanup)
   389→		}
   390→
   391→		states = append(states, state)
   392→	}
   393→	return states, nil
   394→}
   395→
   396→// stateFilePath returns the path to a session state file.
   397→func (s *StateStore) stateFilePath(sessionID string) string {
   398→	return filepath.Join(s.stateDir, sessionID+".json")
   399→}

   401→// gitCommonDirCache caches the git common dir to avoid repeated subprocess calls.
   402→// Keyed by working directory to handle directory changes (same pattern as paths.WorktreeRoot).
   403→var (
   404→	gitCommonDirMu       sync.RWMutex
   405→	gitCommonDirCache    string
   406→	gitCommonDirCacheDir string
   407→)
   408→
   409→// ClearGitCommonDirCache clears the cached git common dir.
   410→// Useful for testing when changing directories.
   411→func ClearGitCommonDirCache() {
   412→	gitCommonDirMu.Lock()
   413→	gitCommonDirCache = ""
   414→	gitCommonDirCacheDir = ""
   415→	gitCommonDirMu.Unlock()
   416→}
   417→
   418→// getGitCommonDir returns the path to the shared git directory.
   419→// In a regular checkout, this is .git/
   420→// In a worktree, this is the main repo's .git/ (not .git/worktrees/<name>/)
   421→// The result is cached per working directory.
   422→func getGitCommonDir(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
   423→	cwd, err := os.Getwd() //nolint:forbidigo // used for cache key, not git-relative paths
   424→	if err != nil {
   425→		cwd = ""
   426→	}
   427→
   428→	// Check cache with read lock first
   429→	gitCommonDirMu.RLock()
   430→	if gitCommonDirCache != "" && gitCommonDirCacheDir == cwd {
   431→		cached := gitCommonDirCache
   432→		gitCommonDirMu.RUnlock()
   433→		return cached, nil
   434→	}
   435→	gitCommonDirMu.RUnlock()
   436→
   437→	// Cache miss — resolve via git subprocess
   438→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "rev-parse", "--git-common-dir")
   439→	cmd.Dir = "."
   440→	output, err := cmd.Output()
   441→	if err != nil {
   442→		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to get git common dir: %w", err)
   443→	}
   444→
   445→	commonDir := strings.TrimSpace(string(output))
   446→
   447→	// git rev-parse --git-common-dir returns relative paths from the working directory,
   448→	// so we need to make it absolute if it isn't already
   449→	if !filepath.IsAbs(commonDir) {
   450→		commonDir = filepath.Join(".", commonDir)
   451→	}
   452→	commonDir = filepath.Clean(commonDir)
   453→
   454→	gitCommonDirMu.Lock()
   455→	gitCommonDirCache = commonDir
   456→	gitCommonDirCacheDir = cwd
   457→	gitCommonDirMu.Unlock()
   458→
   459→	return commonDir, nil
   460→}

    12→// TestLogsOnlyRewind_AppearsInRewindList verifies that after user commits with
    13→// shadow hooks, the commits appear in the rewind list as logs-only points.
    14→//
    15→// Workflow:
    16→// 1. Session creates checkpoint
    17→// 2. User commits (triggers condensation, shadow branch pruned)
    18→// 3. Verify commit appears in rewind list with IsLogsOnly=true
    19→func TestLogsOnlyRewind_AppearsInRewindList(t *testing.T) {
    20→	t.Parallel()
    21→	env := NewTestEnv(t)

    23→
    24→	// Setup

    26→	env.WriteFile("README.md", "# Test Repository")

    29→	env.GitCheckoutNewBranch("feature/logs-only-test")
    30→	env.InitEntire()
    31→
    32→	t.Log("Phase 1: Create session and checkpoint")
    33→
    34→	session := env.NewSession()
    35→	if err := env.SimulateUserPromptSubmit(session.ID); err != nil {
    36→		t.Fatalf("SimulateUserPromptSubmit failed: %v", err)
    37→	}
    38→
    39→	// Create a file
    40→	content := "package main\n\nfunc main() {\n\tprintln(\"hello\")\n}\n"
    41→	env.WriteFile("main.go", content)
    42→
    43→	session.CreateTranscript(
    44→		"Create main.go with hello world",
    45→		[]FileChange{{Path: "main.go", Content: content}},
    46→	)
    47→
    48→	if err := env.SimulateStop(session.ID, session.TranscriptPath); err != nil {
    49→		t.Fatalf("SimulateStop failed: %v", err)
    50→	}
    51→
    52→	// Verify checkpoint exists (not logs-only yet)
    53→	points := env.GetRewindPoints()
    54→	if len(points) != 1 {
    55→		t.Fatalf("Expected 1 rewind point before commit, got %d", len(points))
    56→	}
    57→	if points[0].IsLogsOnly {
    58→		t.Error("Before user commit, point should NOT be logs-only (has active checkpoint)")
    59→	}
    60→
    61→	t.Log("Phase 2: User commits (triggers condensation)")
    62→
    63→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add main.go", "main.go")
    64→
    65→	// Get commit hash and condensation ID (now from entire/checkpoints/v1 branch, not commit trailer)
    66→	commitHash := env.GetHeadHash()
    67→	condensationID := env.GetLatestCondensationID()
    68→	t.Logf("Condensation ID: %s", condensationID)
    69→
    70→	t.Log("Phase 3: Verify logs-only point appears in rewind list")
    71→
    72→	// Get rewind points again
    73→	points = env.GetRewindPoints()
    74→
    75→	// Find the logs-only point
    76→	var logsOnlyPoint *RewindPoint
    77→	for i := range points {
    78→		if points[i].IsLogsOnly {
    79→			logsOnlyPoint = &points[i]
    80→			break
    81→		}
    82→	}
    83→
    84→	if logsOnlyPoint == nil {
    85→		t.Fatal("Expected to find a logs-only rewind point after user commit")
    86→	}
    87→
    88→	// Verify logs-only point properties
    89→	if logsOnlyPoint.ID != commitHash {
    90→		t.Errorf("Logs-only point ID should be commit hash %s, got %s", commitHash, logsOnlyPoint.ID)
    91→	}
    92→
    93→	if logsOnlyPoint.CondensationID != condensationID {
    94→		t.Errorf("Logs-only point should have CondensationID %s, got %s", condensationID, logsOnlyPoint.CondensationID)
    95→	}
    96→
    97→	if !strings.Contains(logsOnlyPoint.Message, "Add main.go") {
    98→		t.Errorf("Logs-only point message should contain commit message, got: %s", logsOnlyPoint.Message)
    99→	}
   100→
   101→	t.Logf("Found logs-only point: ID=%s, Message=%s, CondensationID=%s",
   102→		logsOnlyPoint.ID[:7], logsOnlyPoint.Message, logsOnlyPoint.CondensationID)
   103→}

**`findSessionsForCommit()`** at `/Users/pfleidi/entire/cli/.worktrees/fix-squash-merge-rewind/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_session.go` (line 121):

## `entire rewind` — Full Explanation

### What It Does (User Perspective)

**Rewind** lets you roll back your working directory to a previous checkpoint — a snapshot the CLI silently saved while an AI agent was working. Think of it as "undo" for agent sessions.

**Why you'd use it:** An agent made changes you don't like, went down a wrong path, or broke something. Instead of manually reverting files, you pick a checkpoint and the CLI restores everything to that exact state.

### What the User Sees

```
$ entire rewind
```

An interactive TUI appears listing checkpoints (newest first):

```
? Select a rewind point:
  > [2m ago] Session checkpoint #3 — "Add login feature"
    [5m ago] Session checkpoint #2 — "Add login feature"
    [8m ago] Session checkpoint #1 — "Add login feature"
    [1h ago] Committed: abc123 — "Implement auth system"   (logs only)
```

Each entry shows the timestamp, a description, and the session prompt that triggered it. **Regular checkpoints** (from the current uncommitted session) restore both files and transcripts. **Logs-only checkpoints** (from already-committed work) only restore the agent transcript so you can resume the conversation — they don't change files.

If you have uncommitted changes, a warning shows the diff stats but doesn't block:

```
⚠ You have uncommitted changes:
  +12 -3  src/auth.go
  +5  -0  src/auth_test.go
Proceed with rewind? [y/N]
```

After confirming, files are restored:

```
Restored: src/auth.go
Restored: src/auth_test.go
Deleted:  src/temp_file.go  (wasn't in checkpoint)

Rewound to abc1234. Resume with: claude -r 2026-03-04-session-uuid
```

**Non-interactive usage:**

```bash
entire rewind --list              # JSON list of rewind points
entire rewind --to abc1234abc1234 # Direct rewind to specific commit
entire rewind --logs-only         # Only restore transcripts
```

---

### How It Works Under the Covers

#### Layer 1: Checkpoint Creation (during agent work)

Every time the agent completes a turn, the CLI's hook (`Stop` / `PostToolUse`) calls `SaveStep()`, which:

1. Snapshots the entire working directory + metadata into a git tree (in-memory, using go-git plumbing)
2. Commits that tree to a **shadow branch** — never touching the user's actual branch
3. Updates session state in `.git/entire-sessions/<session-id>.json`

The shadow branch is named `entire/<HEAD-hash[:7]>-<worktreeHash[:6]>` (e.g., `entire/d2fd271-a1b2c3`). Each commit on it is a full snapshot of the repo at that checkpoint.

#### Layer 2: Finding Rewind Points

`GetRewindPoints()` does two things:

**A) Shadow branch checkpoints** (uncommitted sessions):
- Reads `.git/entire-sessions/*.json` to find sessions matching the current HEAD
- Walks the shadow branch commit log
- Parses trailers (`Entire-Session`, `Entire-Metadata`) to associate commits with sessions
- Returns these as regular `RewindPoint`s

**B) Logs-only checkpoints** (committed work):
- Scans the current branch history for commits with `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` trailers
- Looks up the corresponding metadata on `entire/checkpoints/v1` orphan branch
- Returns these as `RewindPoint{IsLogsOnly: true}`

Both lists are merged, deduplicated, and sorted newest-first.

#### Layer 3: The Actual Rewind

`Rewind(point)` does **not** use `git reset` or `git checkout`. It manually restores files:

1. **Reset shadow branch pointer** — moves the branch ref to the selected commit (future checkpoints build from here)
2. **Build file sets** — reads the checkpoint commit tree and HEAD tree to know what files exist where
3. **Delete untracked files** that aren't in the checkpoint and weren't present before the session started (protected by `UntrackedFilesAtStart` in session state)
4. **Write every file** from the checkpoint tree to the working directory with `os.WriteFile()`, creating directories as needed
5. **Restore the agent transcript** — writes the session transcript (`.jsonl`) to the agent's session directory so the user can resume with `claude -r <session-id>`

HEAD and branch pointer are untouched. The user's git history is never modified.

---

### Deep Dive: On-Disk Structures

#### 1. Session State Files

**Location:** `.git/entire-sessions/<session-id>.json`

```json
{
  "session_id": "2026-03-04-a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",
  "base_commit": "d2fd2710abc123def456789012345678abcdef01",
  "worktree_id": "a1b2c3",
  "step_count": 3,
  "phase": "IDLE",
  "agent_type": "claude-code",
  "untracked_files_at_start": ["notes.txt", "scratch/ideas.md"],
  "last_interaction": "2026-03-04T10:30:00Z",
  "created_at": "2026-03-04T10:00:00Z"
}
```

These are the lightweight state files that track active sessions. They're used to find which shadow branch to look at.

#### 2. Shadow Branch Commits

**Branch:** `entire/d2fd271-a1b2c3` (7-char HEAD hash + 6-char worktree hash)

Each commit on this branch contains:

```
<full working directory snapshot>
├── src/
│   ├── auth.go              # Exact file contents at this checkpoint
│   └── auth_test.go
├── go.mod
├── go.sum
└── .entire/metadata/<session-id>/
    ├── full.jsonl            # Agent transcript (JSONL format)
    ├── prompt.txt            # User prompts for this checkpoint window
    └── tasks/<tool-use-id>/  # (if task checkpoint)
        ├── checkpoint.json   # {"checkpoint_uuid": "...", "tool_use_id": "..."}
        └── agent-<id>.jsonl  # Subagent transcript
```

**Commit trailers:**
```
Entire-Session: 2026-03-04-a1b2c3d4-...
Entire-Metadata: .entire/metadata/2026-03-04-a1b2c3d4-...
Entire-Strategy: manual-commit

├── metadata.json
├── 0/                        # First session (0-indexed)
│   ├── metadata.json         # Session-specific metadata
│   ├── full.jsonl            # Transcript

│   └── full.jsonl
└── ...

  "session_count": 2,
  "strategy": "manual-commit",
  "created_at": "2026-03-04T10:35:00Z",
  "files_touched": ["src/auth.go", "src/auth_test.go"]
}
```

**Session-level `metadata.json` (inside `0/`, `1/`, etc.):**
```json
{
  "session_id": "2026-03-04-session-1",
  "agent": "Claude Code",
  "files_touched": ["src/auth.go"],
  "created_at": "2026-03-04T10:00:00Z"
}
```

The user's commit on their branch gets an `Entire-Checkpoint: a3b2c4d5e6f7` trailer, creating bidirectional linking between the user's commit and the metadata.

#### 4. Transcript Format (`full.jsonl`)

Each line is a JSON object representing one interaction turn — the exact format depends on the agent but typically includes role, content, tool calls, and timestamps.

#### 5. The `RewindPoint` Struct

The Go struct that ties it all together:

```go
type RewindPoint struct {
    ID               string          // 40-char commit hash (shadow or user commit)
    Message          string          // Human-readable label
    MetadataDir      string          // Path within tree (e.g., ".entire/metadata/<sid>")
    Date             time.Time
    IsTaskCheckpoint bool
    ToolUseID        string
    IsLogsOnly       bool            // true = committed, no file restore
    CheckpointID     id.CheckpointID // 12-hex-char ID for logs-only
    Agent            types.AgentType
    SessionID        string
    SessionPrompt    string          // First user prompt (for display)
}
```

---

### Flow Summary

```
Agent works → Stop hook → SaveStep()
  → snapshot working dir + metadata → commit to shadow branch
  → update .git/entire-sessions/<sid>.json

User runs: entire rewind
  → read session states → walk shadow branch → merge with committed checkpoints
  → user picks a point
  → read commit tree → write files to working dir → restore transcript
  → print resume command

User commits → post-commit hook → condense()
  → copy metadata from shadow branch to entire/checkpoints/v1
  → add Entire-Checkpoint trailer to user's commit
  → these become "logs-only" rewind points going forward
```

The key design insight: the shadow branch stores **full working directory snapshots** (not diffs), so rewind is a simple tree-read-and-write operation. The user's branch is never touched — no commits, no resets, no history rewriting.

    38→// hasTTY checks if /dev/tty is available for interactive prompts.
    39→// Returns false when running as an agent subprocess (no controlling terminal).
    40→//

    42→//   - ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1 → simulate human (TTY available)
    43→//   - ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0 → simulate agent (no TTY)
    44→func hasTTY() bool {
    45→	if v := os.Getenv("ENTIRE_TEST_TTY"); v != "" {
    46→		return v == "1"
    47→	}

    49→	// Gemini CLI sets GEMINI_CLI=1 when running shell commands.
    50→	// Gemini subprocesses may have access to the user's TTY, but they can't
    51→	// actually respond to interactive prompts. Treat them as non-TTY.
    52→	// See: https://geminicli.com/docs/tools/shell/
    53→	if os.Getenv("GEMINI_CLI") != "" {

    58→	// Factory AI Droid (and other non-interactive environments like CI) set this.

    60→	// git prompting, our hook shouldn't prompt either.
    61→	if os.Getenv("GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT") == "0" {
    62→		return false

    73→// ttyResult represents the outcome of a TTY confirmation prompt.

    82→// askConfirmTTY prompts the user via /dev/tty whether to link a commit to session context.
    83→// This requires a controlling terminal — callers must check hasTTY() first and handle
    84→// the no-TTY case (agent subprocesses, CI) themselves.
    85→//
    86→// header is displayed as the first line (e.g., "Entire: Active Claude Code session").
    87→// detail lines are displayed indented below the header.
    88→func askConfirmTTY(header string, details []string, prompt string, defaultYes bool) ttyResult {

    92→	}

    96→	// but we can't actually read from the TTY in tests.
    97→	if os.Getenv("ENTIRE_TEST_TTY") != "" {
    98→		return defaultResult

   102→	// This is the controlling terminal, which works even when stdin/stderr are redirected
   103→	// (e.g., human runs git commit -m where stdin is not a pipe).

   122→	}

   125→	reader := bufio.NewReader(tty)
   126→	response, err := reader.ReadString('\n')
   127→	if err != nil {

   129→	}

   132→	switch response {
   133→	case "y", "yes":

   148→// local settings file doesn't exist yet.

   152→		return fmt.Errorf("resolving local settings path: %w", err)

   156→	// If the file doesn't exist, start with an empty map so we only write commit_linking.

   173→	if err != nil {

   188→// CommitMsg is called by the git commit-msg hook after the user edits the message.
   189→// If the message contains only our trailer (no actual user content), strip it
   190→// so git will abort the commit due to empty message.
   191→
   192→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) CommitMsg(_ context.Context, commitMsgFile string) error { //nolint:unparam // error return is part of the hook contract; callers check it
   193→	content, err := os.ReadFile(commitMsgFile) //nolint:gosec // Path comes from git hook
   194→	if err != nil {
   195→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   196→	}
   197→
   198→	message := string(content)
   199→
   200→	// Check if our trailer is present (ParseCheckpoint validates format, so found==true means valid)
   201→	if _, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(message); !found {
   202→		// No trailer, nothing to do
   203→		return nil
   204→	}
   205→
   206→	// Check if there's any user content (non-comment, non-trailer lines)
   207→	if !hasUserContent(message) {
   208→		// No user content - strip the trailer so git aborts
   209→		message = stripCheckpointTrailer(message)
   210→		if err := os.WriteFile(commitMsgFile, []byte(message), 0o600); err != nil {
   211→			return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   212→		}
   213→	}
   214→
   215→	return nil
   216→}

   218→// hasUserContent checks if the message has any content besides comments and our trailer.
   219→func hasUserContent(message string) bool {
   220→	trailerPrefix := trailers.CheckpointTrailerKey + ":"
   221→	for _, line := range strings.Split(message, "\n") {
   222→		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
   223→		// Skip empty lines
   224→		if trimmed == "" {
   225→			continue
   226→		}
   227→		// Skip comment lines
   228→		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "#") {
   229→			continue
   230→		}
   231→		// Skip our trailer line
   232→		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, trailerPrefix) {
   233→			continue
   234→		}
   235→		// Found user content
   236→		return true
   237→	}
   238→	return false
   239→}
   240→
   241→// stripCheckpointTrailer removes the Entire-Checkpoint trailer line from the message.
   242→func stripCheckpointTrailer(message string) string {
   243→	trailerPrefix := trailers.CheckpointTrailerKey + ":"
   244→	var result []string
   245→	for _, line := range strings.Split(message, "\n") {
   246→		if !strings.HasPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(line), trailerPrefix) {
   247→			result = append(result, line)
   248→		}
   249→	}
   250→	return strings.Join(result, "\n")

   252→
   253→// isGitSequenceOperation checks if git is currently in the middle of a rebase,
   254→// cherry-pick, or revert operation. During these operations, commits are being
   255→// replayed and should not be linked to agent sessions.
   256→//
   257→// Detects:
   258→//   - rebase: .git/rebase-merge/ or .git/rebase-apply/ directories
   259→//   - cherry-pick: .git/CHERRY_PICK_HEAD file
   260→//   - revert: .git/REVERT_HEAD file
   261→func isGitSequenceOperation(ctx context.Context) bool {
   262→	// Get git directory (handles worktrees and relative paths correctly)
   263→	gitDir, err := GetGitDir(ctx)
   264→	if err != nil {
   265→		return false // Can't determine, assume not in sequence operation
   266→	}
   267→
   268→	// Check for rebase state directories
   269→	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(gitDir, "rebase-merge")); err == nil {
   270→		return true
   271→	}
   272→	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(gitDir, "rebase-apply")); err == nil {
   273→		return true
   274→	}
   275→
   276→	// Check for cherry-pick and revert state files
   277→	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(gitDir, "CHERRY_PICK_HEAD")); err == nil {
   278→		return true
   279→	}
   280→	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(gitDir, "REVERT_HEAD")); err == nil {
   281→		return true
   282→	}
   283→
   284→	return false
   285→}
   286→
   287→// PrepareCommitMsg is called by the git prepare-commit-msg hook.
   288→// Adds an Entire-Checkpoint trailer to the commit message with a stable checkpoint ID.
   289→// Only adds a trailer if there's actually new session content to condense.
   290→// The actual condensation happens in PostCommit - if the user removes the trailer,
   291→// the commit will not be linked to the session (useful for "manual" commits).
   292→// For amended commits, preserves the existing checkpoint ID.
   293→//
   294→// The source parameter indicates how the commit was initiated:
   295→//   - "" or "template": normal editor flow - adds trailer with explanatory comment
   296→//   - "message": using -m or -F flag - prompts user interactively via /dev/tty
   297→//   - "merge", "squash": skip trailer entirely (auto-generated messages)
   298→//   - "commit": amend operation - preserves existing trailer or restores from LastCheckpointID
   299→//
   300→
   301→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) PrepareCommitMsg(ctx context.Context, commitMsgFile string, source string) error {
   302→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "checkpoint")
   303→
   304→	// Skip during rebase, cherry-pick, or revert operations
   305→	// These are replaying existing commits and should not be linked to agent sessions
   306→	if isGitSequenceOperation(ctx) {
   307→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: skipped during git sequence operation",
   308→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   309→			slog.String("source", source),
   310→		)
   311→		return nil
   312→	}
   313→
   314→	// Skip for merge and squash sources
   315→	// These are auto-generated messages - not from Claude sessions
   316→	switch source {
   317→	case "merge", "squash":
   318→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: skipped for source",
   319→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   320→			slog.String("source", source),
   321→		)
   322→		return nil
   323→	}
   324→
   325→	// Handle amend (source="commit") separately: preserve or restore trailer
   326→	if source == "commit" {
   327→		return s.handleAmendCommitMsg(ctx, commitMsgFile)
   328→	}
   329→
   330→	repo, err := OpenRepository(ctx)
   331→	if err != nil {
   332→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   333→	}
   334→
   335→	worktreePath, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(ctx)
   336→	if err != nil {
   337→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   338→	}
   339→
   340→	// Find all active sessions for this worktree
   341→	// We match by worktree (not BaseCommit) because the user may have made
   342→	// intermediate commits without entering new prompts, causing HEAD to diverge
   343→	sessions, err := s.findSessionsForWorktree(ctx, worktreePath)
   344→	if err != nil || len(sessions) == 0 {
   345→		// No active sessions or error listing - silently skip (hooks must be resilient)
   346→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: no active sessions",
   347→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   348→			slog.String("source", source),
   349→		)
   350→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Intentional: hooks must be silent on failure
   351→	}
   352→
   353→	// Fast path: when an agent is committing (ACTIVE session + no TTY), skip
   354→	// content detection and interactive prompts. The agent can't respond to TTY
   355→	// prompts and the content detection can miss mid-session work (no shadow
   356→	// branch yet, transcript analysis may fail). Generate a checkpoint ID and
   357→	// add the trailer directly.
   358→	if !hasTTY() {
   359→		for _, state := range sessions {
   360→			if state.Phase.IsActive() {
   361→				return s.addTrailerForAgentCommit(logCtx, commitMsgFile, state, source)
   362→			}
   363→		}
   364→	}
   365→
   366→	// Check if any session has new content to condense
   367→	sessionsWithContent := s.filterSessionsWithNewContent(ctx, repo, sessions)
   368→
   369→	if len(sessionsWithContent) == 0 {
   370→		// No new content — no trailer needed
   371→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: no content to link",
   372→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   373→			slog.String("source", source),
   374→			slog.Int("sessions_found", len(sessions)),
   375→		)
   376→		return nil
   377→	}
   378→
   379→	// Read current commit message

   381→	if err != nil {

   101→// For mid-session commits (no Stop/SaveStep called yet), the shadow branch may not exist.

   145→	// committed in this specific commit. This ensures each checkpoint represents
   146→	// exactly the files in that commit, not all files mentioned in the transcript.
   147→	if len(committedFiles) > 0 {
   148→		hadFilesBeforeFiltering := len(sessionData.FilesTouched) > 0
   149→
   150→		if hadFilesBeforeFiltering {
   151→			filtered := make([]string, 0, len(sessionData.FilesTouched))
   152→			for _, f := range sessionData.FilesTouched {
   153→				if _, ok := committedFiles[f]; ok {
   154→					filtered = append(filtered, f)

   171→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get checkpoint store: %w", err)

   235→		CheckpointID:                checkpointID,
   236→		SessionID:                   state.SessionID,
   237→		Strategy:                    StrategyNameManualCommit,
   238→		Branch:                      branchName,
   239→		Transcript:                  sessionData.Transcript,
   240→		Prompts:                     sessionData.Prompts,
   241→		FilesTouched:                sessionData.FilesTouched,
   242→		CheckpointsCount:            state.StepCount,
   243→		EphemeralBranch:             shadowBranchName,
   244→		AuthorName:                  authorName,
   245→		AuthorEmail:                 authorEmail,

   247→		TurnID:                      state.TurnID,
   248→		TranscriptIdentifierAtStart: state.TranscriptIdentifierAtStart,
   249→		CheckpointTranscriptStart:   state.CheckpointTranscriptStart,

   277→func calculateSessionAttributions(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, shadowRef *plumbing.Reference, sessionData *ExtractedSessionData, state *SessionState, opts ...attributionOpts) *cpkg.InitialAttribution {
   278→	// Calculate initial attribution using accumulated prompt attribution data.
   279→	// This uses user edits captured at each prompt start (before agent works),
   280→	// plus any user edits after the final checkpoint (shadow → head).
   281→	//
   282→	// When shadowRef is nil (agent committed mid-turn before SaveStep),
   283→	// HEAD is used as the shadow tree. This is correct because the agent's
   284→	// commit IS HEAD — there are no user edits between agent work and commit.
   285→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "attribution")
   286→
   287→	var o attributionOpts
   288→	if len(opts) > 0 {
   289→		o = opts[0]
   290→	}
   291→
   292→	headTree := o.headTree
   293→	if headTree == nil {
   294→		headRef, headErr := repo.Head()
   295→		if headErr != nil {
   296→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "attribution skipped: failed to get HEAD",
   297→				slog.String("error", headErr.Error()))
   298→			return nil
   299→		}
   300→
   301→		headCommit, commitErr := repo.CommitObject(headRef.Hash())
   302→		if commitErr != nil {
   303→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "attribution skipped: failed to get HEAD commit",
   304→				slog.String("error", commitErr.Error()))
   305→			return nil
   306→		}
   307→
   308→		var treeErr error
   309→		headTree, treeErr = headCommit.Tree()
   310→		if treeErr != nil {
   311→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "attribution skipped: failed to get HEAD tree",
   312→				slog.String("error", treeErr.Error()))
   313→			return nil
   314→		}
   315→	}
   316→
   317→	// Get shadow tree: from pre-resolved cache, shadow branch, or HEAD (agent committed directly).
   318→	shadowTree := o.shadowTree
   319→	if shadowTree == nil {
   320→		if shadowRef != nil {
   321→			shadowCommit, shadowErr := repo.CommitObject(shadowRef.Hash())
   322→			if shadowErr != nil {
   323→				logging.Debug(logCtx, "attribution skipped: failed to get shadow commit",
   324→					slog.String("error", shadowErr.Error()),
   325→					slog.String("shadow_ref", shadowRef.Hash().String()))
   326→				return nil
   327→			}
   328→			var shadowTreeErr error
   329→			shadowTree, shadowTreeErr = shadowCommit.Tree()
   330→			if shadowTreeErr != nil {
   331→				logging.Debug(logCtx, "attribution skipped: failed to get shadow tree",
   332→					slog.String("error", shadowTreeErr.Error()))
   333→				return nil
   334→			}
   335→		} else {
   336→			// No shadow branch: agent committed mid-turn. Use HEAD as shadow
   337→			// because the agent's work is the commit itself.
   338→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "attribution: using HEAD as shadow (no shadow branch)")
   339→			shadowTree = headTree
   340→		}
   341→	}
   342→
   343→	// Get base tree (state before session started)
   344→	var baseTree *object.Tree
   345→	attrBase := state.AttributionBaseCommit
   346→	if attrBase == "" {
   347→		attrBase = state.BaseCommit // backward compat
   348→	}
   349→	if baseCommit, baseErr := repo.CommitObject(plumbing.NewHash(attrBase)); baseErr == nil {
   350→		if tree, baseTErr := baseCommit.Tree(); baseTErr == nil {
   351→			baseTree = tree
   352→		} else {
   353→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "attribution: base tree unavailable",
   354→				slog.String("error", baseTErr.Error()))
   355→		}
   356→	} else {
   357→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "attribution: base commit unavailable",
   358→			slog.String("error", baseErr.Error()),
   359→			slog.String("attribution_base", attrBase))
   360→	}
   361→
   362→	// Log accumulated prompt attributions for debugging
   363→	var totalUserAdded, totalUserRemoved int
   364→	for i, pa := range state.PromptAttributions {
   365→		totalUserAdded += pa.UserLinesAdded
   366→		totalUserRemoved += pa.UserLinesRemoved
   367→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution data",
   368→			slog.Int("checkpoint", pa.CheckpointNumber),
   369→			slog.Int("user_added", pa.UserLinesAdded),
   370→			slog.Int("user_removed", pa.UserLinesRemoved),
   371→			slog.Int("agent_added", pa.AgentLinesAdded),
   372→			slog.Int("agent_removed", pa.AgentLinesRemoved),
   373→			slog.Int("index", i))
   374→	}
   375→
   376→	attribution := CalculateAttributionWithAccumulated(
   377→		ctx,
   378→		baseTree,
   379→		shadowTree,
   380→		headTree,
   381→		sessionData.FilesTouched,
   382→		state.PromptAttributions,
   383→		o.repoDir,
   384→		o.attributionBaseCommit,
   385→		o.headCommitHash,
   386→	)
   387→
   388→	if attribution != nil {
   389→		logging.Info(logCtx, "attribution calculated",
   390→			slog.Int("agent_lines", attribution.AgentLines),
   391→			slog.Int("human_added", attribution.HumanAdded),
   392→			slog.Int("human_modified", attribution.HumanModified),
   393→			slog.Int("human_removed", attribution.HumanRemoved),
   394→			slog.Int("total_committed", attribution.TotalCommitted),
   395→			slog.Float64("agent_percentage", attribution.AgentPercentage),
   396→			slog.Int("accumulated_user_added", totalUserAdded),
   397→			slog.Int("accumulated_user_removed", totalUserRemoved),
   398→			slog.Int("files_touched", len(sessionData.FilesTouched)))
   399→	}
   400→
   401→	return attribution
   402→}

   404→// extractSessionData extracts session data from the shadow branch.
   405→// filesTouched is the list of files tracked during the session (from SessionState.FilesTouched).
   406→// agentType identifies the agent (e.g., "Gemini CLI", "Claude Code") to determine transcript format.
   407→// liveTranscriptPath, when non-empty and readable, is preferred over the shadow branch copy.
   408→// This handles the case where SaveStep was skipped (no code changes) but the transcript
   409→// continued growing — the shadow branch copy would be stale.
   410→// checkpointTranscriptStart is the line offset (Claude) or message index (Gemini) where the current checkpoint began.
   411→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) extractSessionData(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, shadowRef plumbing.Hash, sessionID string, filesTouched []string, agentType types.AgentType, liveTranscriptPath string, checkpointTranscriptStart int, isActive bool) (*ExtractedSessionData, error) {
   412→	ag, _ := agent.GetByAgentType(agentType) //nolint:errcheck // ag may be nil for unknown agent types; callers use type assertions so nil is safe
   413→	commit, err := repo.CommitObject(shadowRef)
   414→	if err != nil {
   415→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit object: %w", err)
   416→	}
   417→
   418→	tree, err := commit.Tree()
   419→	if err != nil {
   420→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit tree: %w", err)
   421→	}
   422→
   423→	data := &ExtractedSessionData{}
   424→	// sessionID is already an "entire session ID" (with date prefix)
   425→	metadataDir := paths.SessionMetadataDirFromSessionID(sessionID)
   426→
   427→	// Extract transcript — prefer the live file when available, fall back to shadow branch.
   428→	// The shadow branch copy may be stale if the last turn ended without code changes
   429→	// (SaveStep is only called when there are file modifications).
   430→	var fullTranscript string
   431→	if liveTranscriptPath != "" {
   432→		// Ensure transcript file exists (OpenCode creates it lazily via `opencode export`).
   433→		// Only wait for flush when the session is active — for idle/ended sessions the
   434→		// transcript is already fully flushed (the Stop hook completed the flush).
   435→		if isActive {
   436→			prepareTranscriptIfNeeded(ctx, ag, liveTranscriptPath)
   437→		}
   438→		if liveData, readErr := os.ReadFile(liveTranscriptPath); readErr == nil && len(liveData) > 0 { //nolint:gosec // path from session state
   439→			fullTranscript = string(liveData)
   440→		}
   441→	}
   442→	if fullTranscript == "" {
   443→		// Fall back to shadow branch copy
   444→		if file, fileErr := tree.File(metadataDir + "/" + paths.TranscriptFileName); fileErr == nil {
   445→			if content, contentErr := file.Contents(); contentErr == nil {
   446→				fullTranscript = content
   447→			}
   448→		} else if file, fileErr := tree.File(metadataDir + "/" + paths.TranscriptFileNameLegacy); fileErr == nil {
   449→			if content, contentErr := file.Contents(); contentErr == nil {
   450→				fullTranscript = content
   451→			}
   452→		}
   453→	}
   454→
   455→	// Process transcript based on agent type
   456→	if fullTranscript != "" {
   457→		data.Transcript = []byte(fullTranscript)
   458→		data.FullTranscriptLines = countTranscriptItems(agentType, fullTranscript)
   459→		// Read prompts from shadow branch tree (source of truth after SaveStep)
   460→		if file, fileErr := tree.File(metadataDir + "/" + paths.PromptFileName); fileErr == nil {
   461→			if content, contentErr := file.Contents(); contentErr == nil && content != "" {
   462→				data.Prompts = splitPromptContent(content)
   463→			}
   464→		}
   465→		// Filesystem fallback (written at turn start, covers mid-turn commits)
   466→		if len(data.Prompts) == 0 {
   467→			data.Prompts = readPromptsFromFilesystem(ctx, sessionID)
   468→		}
   469→	}
   470→
   471→	// Use tracked files from session state (not all files in tree)
   472→	data.FilesTouched = filesTouched
   473→

   658→func (h *postCommitActionHandler) shouldCondenseWithOverlapCheck(isActive bool, lastInteraction *time.Time) bool {
   659→	if !h.hasNew {
   660→		return false
   661→	}

   663→	// PrepareCommitMsg already validated this commit is session-related
   664→	// (added trailer). The overlap check is only meaningful when we need
   665→	// heuristic evidence that a commit was related to the session.
   666→	//

   669→	// session has no recent interaction and falls through to the overlap check.
   670→	if isActive && isRecentInteraction(lastInteraction) {

   672→	}

   674→		return false // No files tracked = no overlap evidence
   675→	}

   678→	// would pass the "modified file" check in filesOverlapWithContent
   679→	// (because the file exists in the parent tree), causing stale
   680→	// sessions to be incorrectly condensed.
   681→	var committedTouchedFiles []string

## Analysis: Squash Merge + Rewind Failure Mode

### 1. How `GetLogsOnlyRewindPoints()` works

**File:** `/Users/pfleidi/entire/cli/.worktrees/fix-squash-merge-rewind/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_rewind.go`, lines 136-251

The function:
1. Calls `s.listCheckpoints(ctx)` to get all checkpoints from `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch
2. Builds a map of `checkpointID -> CheckpointInfo`
3. Walks the current branch's commit history (up to `logsOnlyScanLimit = 50` commits, defined in `manual_commit_types.go` line 15)
4. For each commit, calls `trailers.ParseCheckpoint(c.Message)` to extract a single `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer
5. Looks up that checkpoint ID in the map
6. If found, creates a `RewindPoint` with `IsLogsOnly: true`

**Critical detail:** At line 192, it calls `trailers.ParseCheckpoint()` -- the **singular** version.

### 2. How `ParseCheckpoint` works (only finds the FIRST trailer)

**File:** `/Users/pfleidi/entire/cli/.worktrees/fix-squash-merge-rewind/cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go`, lines 129-139

```go
func ParseCheckpoint(commitMessage string) (checkpointID.CheckpointID, bool) {
    matches := checkpointTrailerRegex.FindStringSubmatch(commitMessage)
    if len(matches) > 1 {
        idStr := strings.TrimSpace(matches[1])
        if cpID, err := checkpointID.NewCheckpointID(idStr); err == nil {
            return cpID, true
        }
    }
    return checkpointID.EmptyCheckpointID, false
}
```

`FindStringSubmatch` returns **only the first match**. So if a commit message contains multiple `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers, only the first one is found.

Note: A `ParseAllCheckpoints` function **already exists** (lines 145-165) that uses `FindAllStringSubmatch` and returns all checkpoint IDs, with deduplication. Its comment even says: *"This is useful for squash merge commits that contain multiple Entire-Checkpoint trailers."* However, **it is never called from the strategy package** -- my grep for `ParseAllCheckpoints` in the strategy directory returned zero results.

### 3. What happens during a squash merge

When git performs a squash merge of commits A (trailer: `aaa`), B (trailer: `bbb`), C (trailer: `ccc`), the resulting squash merge commit message depends on the git behavior:

- **Default `git merge --squash`**: Git concatenates all commit messages from the squashed commits. So the squash merge message will contain **all three trailers**: `Entire-Checkpoint: aaa`, `Entire-Checkpoint: bbb`, `Entire-Checkpoint: ccc`.
- **GitHub "Squash and Merge" button**: GitHub also concatenates the commit messages (shown as bullet points). All three trailers would appear in the message body.

### 4. How the `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer is added (prepare-commit-msg)

**File:** `/Users/pfleidi/entire/cli/.worktrees/fix-squash-merge-rewind/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go`, lines 301-478

Key behavior at lines 316-323:
```go
switch source {
case "merge", "squash":
    logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: skipped for source",...)
    return nil
}
```

The `prepare-commit-msg` hook **skips entirely** for `source="merge"` or `source="squash"`. This means:
- When someone runs `git merge --squash feature-branch && git commit`, the prepare-commit-msg hook is called with `source=""` (normal editor flow), so it **would** add a new trailer if there's an active session

## What Happens Today: Only the First Checkpoint Survives

### The Scenario

A developer works with an agent on a feature branch, making three commits:

```
A — "Add auth model"        Entire-Checkpoint: aaa111bbb222
B — "Add auth endpoints"    Entire-Checkpoint: ccc333ddd444
C — "Add auth tests"        Entire-Checkpoint: eee555fff666
```

Each commit triggers `PostCommit`, which condenses session data to `entire/checkpoints/v1`. All three checkpoint IDs (`aaa111bbb222`, `ccc333ddd444`, `eee555fff666`) are safely stored on the metadata branch.

Then the developer does a squash merge into main. Git concatenates the commit messages, so the squash commit contains all three trailers:

```
Add auth system (#42)

* Add auth model

Entire-Checkpoint: aaa111bbb222

* Add auth endpoints

Entire-Checkpoint: ccc333ddd444

* Add auth tests

Entire-Checkpoint: eee555fff666
```

### The Bug

`GetLogsOnlyRewindPoints()` walks the branch history and, for each commit, calls `trailers.ParseCheckpoint()`:

```go
// manual_commit_rewind.go:192
checkpointID, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(c.Message)
```

Which uses `FindStringSubmatch` — **returns only the first match**:

```go
// trailers.go:130
matches := checkpointTrailerRegex.FindStringSubmatch(commitMessage)
```

Result: Only `aaa111bbb222` is found. The squash merge commit appears as **one** rewind point. Checkpoints `ccc333ddd444` and `eee555fff666` are silently lost — the data still exists on `entire/checkpoints/v1`, but no commit in the current history links to them.

**The user loses access to 2 out of 3 checkpoints.**

### The Fix Is Half-Written

`trailers.ParseAllCheckpoints()` already exists at `trailers.go:145` and even has a doc comment saying:

> *"This is useful for squash merge commits that contain multiple Entire-Checkpoint trailers."*

It uses `FindAllStringSubmatch` and returns all checkpoint IDs with deduplication. But it's **never called from the strategy package** — `GetLogsOnlyRewindPoints()` still uses the singular `ParseCheckpoint()`.

   166→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Found %d checkpoints for commit %s but metadata is not available\n",
   167→				len(result.checkpointIDs), result.commitHash[:7])
   168→			return checkRemoteMetadata(ctx, repo, result.checkpointIDs[0])
   169→		}
   170→		skipped := len(result.checkpointIDs) - 1
   171→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Found %d checkpoints for commit %s, resuming from the latest (%d older checkpoints skipped)\n",
   172→			len(result.checkpointIDs), result.commitHash[:7], skipped)
   173→		checkpointID = latest
   174→		metadataTree = tree
   175→	}
   176→
   177→	// Get metadata branch tree for lookups (reuse from resolveLatestCheckpoint if available)
   178→	if metadataTree == nil {
   179→		var err error
   180→		metadataTree, err = strategy.GetMetadataBranchTree(repo)
   181→		if err != nil {
   182→			// No local metadata branch, check if remote has it
   183→			return checkRemoteMetadata(ctx, repo, checkpointID)
   184→		}
   185→	}
   186→
   187→	// Look up metadata from sharded path
   188→	metadata, err := strategy.ReadCheckpointMetadata(metadataTree, checkpointID.Path())
   189→	if err != nil {
   190→		// Checkpoint exists in commit but no local metadata - check remote
   191→		return checkRemoteMetadata(ctx, repo, checkpointID)
   192→	}
   193→
   194→	return resumeSession(ctx, metadata, force)
   195→}
   196→
   197→// resolveLatestCheckpoint reads metadata for each checkpoint ID and returns
   198→// the one with the latest CreatedAt, along with the metadata tree for reuse.
   199→// It tries the local metadata branch first, then fetches from remote, then
   200→// falls back to the remote tree directly.
   201→func resolveLatestCheckpoint(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, checkpointIDs []id.CheckpointID) (id.CheckpointID, *object.Tree, error) {
   202→	metadataTree, err := getMetadataTree(ctx, repo)
   203→	if err != nil {
   204→		return id.EmptyCheckpointID, nil, err
   205→	}
   206→	sorted := collectCheckpointsByAge(metadataTree, checkpointIDs)
   207→	if len(sorted) == 0 {
   208→		return id.EmptyCheckpointID, nil, errors.New("no checkpoint metadata found")
   209→	}
   210→	return sorted[len(sorted)-1].CheckpointID, metadataTree, nil
   211→}
   212→
   213→// getMetadataTree returns the metadata branch tree, trying local first,
   214→// then fetching from remote, then falling back to the remote tree directly.
   215→func getMetadataTree(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository) (*object.Tree, error) {
   216→	metadataTree, err := strategy.GetMetadataBranchTree(repo)
   217→	if err == nil {
   218→		return metadataTree, nil
   219→	}
   220→
   221→	// Try fetching from remote
   222→	if fetchErr := FetchMetadataBranch(ctx); fetchErr == nil {
   223→		metadataTree, err = strategy.GetMetadataBranchTree(repo)
   224→		if err == nil {
   225→			return metadataTree, nil
   226→		}
   227→	}
   228→
   229→	// Try remote tree directly
   230→	remoteTree, remoteErr := strategy.GetRemoteMetadataBranchTree(repo)
   231→	if remoteErr != nil {
   232→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("metadata branch not available: %w", remoteErr)
   233→	}
   234→	return remoteTree, nil
   235→}
   236→
   237→// collectCheckpointsByAge reads metadata for each checkpoint ID from the tree,
   238→// skips any that can't be read, and returns them sorted by CreatedAt ascending.
   239→// Sorting ensures the newest checkpoint is restored last and wins on disk,
   240→// regardless of trailer order in the commit message.
   241→func collectCheckpointsByAge(tree *object.Tree, checkpointIDs []id.CheckpointID) []*strategy.CheckpointInfo {
   242→	var checkpoints []*strategy.CheckpointInfo
   243→	for _, cpID := range checkpointIDs {
   244→		metadata, err := strategy.ReadCheckpointMetadata(tree, cpID.Path())
   245→		if err != nil {
   246→			continue
   247→		}
   248→		checkpoints = append(checkpoints, metadata)
   249→	}
   250→	sort.Slice(checkpoints, func(i, j int) bool {
   251→		return checkpoints[i].CreatedAt.Before(checkpoints[j].CreatedAt)
   252→	})
   253→	return checkpoints
   254→}

   256→// branchCheckpointsResult contains the result of searching for checkpoints on a branch.
   257→type branchCheckpointsResult struct {
   258→	checkpointIDs     []id.CheckpointID
   259→	commitHash        string
   260→	commitMessage     string
   261→	newerCommitsExist bool // true if there are branch-only commits (not merge commits) without checkpoints
   262→	newerCommitCount  int  // count of branch-only commits without checkpoints
   263→}
   264→
   265→// findBranchCheckpoints finds the most recent commit with an Entire-Checkpoint trailer
   266→// among commits that are unique to this branch (not reachable from the default branch).
   267→// This handles the case where main has been merged into the feature branch.
   268→func findBranchCheckpoints(repo *git.Repository, branchName string) (*branchCheckpointsResult, error) {
   269→	result := &branchCheckpointsResult{}
   270→
   271→	// Get HEAD commit
   272→	head, err := repo.Head()
   273→	if err != nil {
   274→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get HEAD: %w", err)
   275→	}
   276→
   277→	headCommit, err := repo.CommitObject(head.Hash())
   278→	if err != nil {
   279→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get HEAD commit: %w", err)
   280→	}
   281→
   282→	// First, check if HEAD itself has a checkpoint (most common case)
   283→	if cpIDs := trailers.ParseAllCheckpoints(headCommit.Message); len(cpIDs) > 0 {
   284→		result.checkpointIDs = cpIDs
   285→		result.commitHash = head.Hash().String()
   286→		result.commitMessage = headCommit.Message
   287→		result.newerCommitsExist = false
   288→		return result, nil
   289→	}
   290→
   291→	// HEAD doesn't have a checkpoint - find branch-only commits
   292→	// Get the default branch name
   293→	defaultBranch := getDefaultBranchFromRemote(repo)
   294→	if defaultBranch == "" {
   295→		// Fallback: try common names
   296→		for _, name := range []string{"main", "master"} {
   297→			if _, err := repo.Reference(plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(name), true); err == nil {
   298→				defaultBranch = name
   299→				break
   300→			}
   301→		}
   302→	}
   303→
   304→	// If we can't find a default branch, or we're on it, just walk all commits
   305→	if defaultBranch == "" || defaultBranch == branchName {
   306→		return findCheckpointInHistory(headCommit, nil), nil
   307→	}
   308→
   309→	// Get the default branch reference
   310→	defaultRef, err := repo.Reference(plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(defaultBranch), true)
   311→	if err != nil {
   312→		// Default branch doesn't exist locally, fall back to walking all commits
   313→		return findCheckpointInHistory(headCommit, nil), nil //nolint:nilerr // Intentional fallback
   314→	}
   315→
   316→	defaultCommit, err := repo.CommitObject(defaultRef.Hash())
   317→	if err != nil {
   318→		// Can't get default commit, fall back to walking all commits
   319→		return findCheckpointInHistory(headCommit, nil), nil //nolint:nilerr // Intentional fallback
   320→	}
   321→
   322→	// Find merge base
   323→	mergeBase, err := headCommit.MergeBase(defaultCommit)
   324→	if err != nil || len(mergeBase) == 0 {
   325→		// No common ancestor, fall back to walking all commits
   326→		return findCheckpointInHistory(headCommit, nil), nil //nolint:nilerr // Intentional fallback
   327→	}
   328→
   329→	// Walk from HEAD to merge base, looking for checkpoint
   330→	return findCheckpointInHistory(headCommit, &mergeBase[0].Hash), nil
   331→}
   332→
   333→// findCheckpointInHistory walks commit history from start looking for a checkpoint trailer.
   334→// If stopAt is provided, stops when reaching that commit (exclusive).
   335→// Returns the first checkpoint found and info about commits between HEAD and the checkpoint.
   336→// It distinguishes between merge commits (bringing in other branches) and regular commits
   337→// (actual branch work) to avoid false warnings after merging main.
   338→func findCheckpointInHistory(start *object.Commit, stopAt *plumbing.Hash) *branchCheckpointsResult {
   339→	result := &branchCheckpointsResult{}
   340→	branchWorkCommits := 0 // Regular commits without checkpoints (actual work)
   341→	const maxCommits = 100 // Limit search depth
   342→	totalChecked := 0
   343→
   344→	current := start
   345→	for current != nil && totalChecked < maxCommits {
   346→		// Stop if we've reached the boundary
   347→		if stopAt != nil && current.Hash == *stopAt {
   348→			break
   349→		}
   350→
   351→		// Check for checkpoint trailer
   352→		if cpIDs := trailers.ParseAllCheckpoints(current.Message); len(cpIDs) > 0 {
   353→			result.checkpointIDs = cpIDs
   354→			result.commitHash = current.Hash.String()
   355→			result.commitMessage = current.Message
   356→			// Only warn about branch work commits, not merge commits
   357→			result.newerCommitsExist = branchWorkCommits > 0
   358→			result.newerCommitCount = branchWorkCommits
   359→			return result
   360→		}
   361→
   362→		// Only count regular commits (not merge commits) as "branch work"
   363→		if current.NumParents() <= 1 {
   364→			branchWorkCommits++
   365→		}
   366→
   367→		totalChecked++
   368→
   369→		// Move to parent (first parent for merge commits - follows the main line)
   370→		if current.NumParents() == 0 {
   371→			break
   372→		}
   373→		parent, err := current.Parent(0)
   374→		if err != nil {
   375→			// Can't get parent, treat as end of history
   376→			break
   377→		}
   378→		current = parent
   379→	}
   380→
   381→	// No checkpoint found
   382→	return result
   383→}

   407→// checkRemoteMetadata checks if checkpoint metadata exists on origin/entire/checkpoints/v1
   408→// and automatically fetches it if available.
   409→func checkRemoteMetadata(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, checkpointID id.CheckpointID) error {
   410→	// Try to get remote metadata branch tree
   411→	remoteTree, err := strategy.GetRemoteMetadataBranchTree(repo)
   412→	if err != nil {
   413→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Checkpoint '%s' found in commit but session metadata not available\n", checkpointID)
   414→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "The entire/checkpoints/v1 branch may not exist locally or on the remote.\n")
   415→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Informational message, not a fatal error
   416→	}
   417→
   418→	// Check if the checkpoint exists on the remote
   419→	metadata, err := strategy.ReadCheckpointMetadata(remoteTree, checkpointID.Path())
   420→	if err != nil {
   421→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Checkpoint '%s' found in commit but session metadata not available\n", checkpointID)
   422→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Informational message, not a fatal error
   423→	}
   424→
   425→	// Metadata exists on remote but not locally - fetch it automatically
   426→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Fetching session metadata from origin...\n")
   427→	if err := FetchMetadataBranch(ctx); err != nil {
   428→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Failed to fetch metadata: %v\n", err)
   429→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "You can try manually: git fetch origin entire/checkpoints/v1:entire/checkpoints/v1\n")
   430→		return NewSilentError(errors.New("failed to fetch metadata"))
   431→	}
   432→
   433→	// Now resume the session with the fetched metadata
   434→	return resumeSession(ctx, metadata, false)
   435→}
