   437→// resumeSession restores and displays the resume command for a specific session.
   438→// For multi-session checkpoints, restores ALL sessions and shows commands for each.
   439→// If force is false, prompts for confirmation when local logs have newer timestamps.
   440→// The caller must provide the already-resolved checkpoint metadata to avoid redundant lookups
   441→// and to support both local and remote metadata trees.
   442→func resumeSession(ctx context.Context, metadata *strategy.CheckpointInfo, force bool) error {
   443→	checkpointID := metadata.CheckpointID
   444→	sessionID := metadata.SessionID
   445→
   446→	// Resolve agent from checkpoint metadata (same as rewind)
   447→	ag, err := strategy.ResolveAgentForRewind(metadata.Agent)
   448→	if err != nil {
   449→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to resolve agent: %w", err)
   450→	}
   451→
   452→	// Initialize logging context with agent
   453→	logCtx := logging.WithAgent(logging.WithComponent(ctx, "resume"), ag.Name())
   454→
   455→	logging.Debug(logCtx, "resume session started",
   456→		slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
   457→		slog.String("session_id", sessionID),
   458→	)
   459→
   460→	// Get worktree root for session directory lookup
   461→	repoRoot, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(ctx)
   462→	if err != nil {
   463→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get worktree root: %w", err)
   464→	}
   465→
   466→	sessionDir, err := ag.GetSessionDir(repoRoot)
   467→	if err != nil {
   468→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to determine session directory: %w", err)
   469→	}
   470→
   471→	// Create directory if it doesn't exist
   472→	if err := os.MkdirAll(sessionDir, 0o700); err != nil {
   473→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to create session directory: %w", err)
   474→	}
   475→
   476→	// Get strategy and restore sessions using full checkpoint data
   477→	strat := GetStrategy(ctx)
   478→
   479→	// Use RestoreLogsOnly via LogsOnlyRestorer interface for multi-session support
   480→	// Create a logs-only rewind point with Agent populated (same as rewind)
   481→	point := strategy.RewindPoint{
   482→		IsLogsOnly:   true,
   483→		CheckpointID: checkpointID,
   484→		Agent:        metadata.Agent,
   485→	}
   486→
   487→	sessions, restoreErr := strat.RestoreLogsOnly(ctx, point, force)
   488→	if restoreErr != nil || len(sessions) == 0 {
   489→		// Fall back to single-session restore (e.g., old checkpoints without agent metadata)
   490→		return resumeSingleSession(ctx, ag, sessionID, checkpointID, repoRoot, force)
   491→	}
   492→
   493→	logging.Debug(logCtx, "resume session completed",
   494→		slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
   495→		slog.Int("session_count", len(sessions)),
   496→	)
   497→
   498→	return displayRestoredSessions(sessions)
   499→}
   500→
   501→// displayRestoredSessions sorts sessions by CreatedAt and prints resume commands.
   502→func displayRestoredSessions(sessions []strategy.RestoredSession) error {
   503→	sort.SliceStable(sessions, func(i, j int) bool {
   504→		return sessions[i].CreatedAt.Before(sessions[j].CreatedAt)
   505→	})
   506→
   507→	if len(sessions) > 1 {
   508→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "\nRestored %d sessions. To continue, run:\n", len(sessions))
   509→	} else if len(sessions) == 1 {
   510→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Session: %s\n", sessions[0].SessionID)
   511→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "\nTo continue this session, run:\n")
   512→	}
   513→
   514→	for i, sess := range sessions {
   515→		sessionAgent, err := strategy.ResolveAgentForRewind(sess.Agent)
   516→		if err != nil {
   517→			return fmt.Errorf("failed to resolve agent for session %s: %w", sess.SessionID, err)
   518→		}
   519→		cmd := sessionAgent.FormatResumeCommand(sess.SessionID)
   520→
   521→		isLast := i == len(sessions)-1
   522→		switch {
   523→		case len(sessions) > 1 && isLast && sess.Prompt != "":
   524→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "  %s  # %s (most recent)\n", cmd, sess.Prompt)
   525→		case len(sessions) > 1 && isLast:
   526→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "  %s  # (most recent)\n", cmd)
   527→		case sess.Prompt != "":
   528→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "  %s  # %s\n", cmd, sess.Prompt)
   529→		default:
   530→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "  %s\n", cmd)
   531→		}
   532→	}
   533→
   534→	return nil
   535→}

   537→// resumeSingleSession restores a single session (fallback when multi-session restore fails).
   538→// Always overwrites existing session logs to ensure consistency with checkpoint state.
   539→// If force is false, prompts for confirmation when local log has newer timestamps.
   540→func resumeSingleSession(ctx context.Context, ag agent.Agent, sessionID string, checkpointID id.CheckpointID, repoRoot string, force bool) error {
   541→	sessionLogPath, err := resolveTranscriptPath(ctx, sessionID, ag)
   542→	if err != nil {
   543→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to resolve transcript path: %w", err)
   544→	}
   545→
   546→	if checkpointID.IsEmpty() {
   547→		logging.Debug(ctx, "resume session: empty checkpoint ID",
   548→			slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
   549→		)
   550→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Session '%s' found in commit trailer but session log not available\n", sessionID)
   551→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "\nTo continue this session, run:\n")
   552→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "  %s\n", ag.FormatResumeCommand(sessionID))
   553→		return nil
   554→	}
   555→
   556→	logContent, _, err := checkpoint.LookupSessionLog(ctx, checkpointID)
   557→	if err != nil {
   558→		if errors.Is(err, checkpoint.ErrCheckpointNotFound) || errors.Is(err, checkpoint.ErrNoTranscript) {
   559→			logging.Debug(ctx, "resume session completed (no metadata)",
   560→				slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
   561→				slog.String("session_id", sessionID),
   562→			)
   563→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Session '%s' found in commit trailer but session log not available\n", sessionID)
   564→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "\nTo continue this session, run:\n")
   565→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "  %s\n", ag.FormatResumeCommand(sessionID))
   566→			return nil
   567→		}
   568→		logging.Error(ctx, "resume session failed",
   569→			slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
   570→			slog.String("session_id", sessionID),
   571→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   572→		)
   573→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get session log: %w", err)
   574→	}
   575→
   576→	// Check if local file has newer timestamps than checkpoint
   577→	if !force {
   578→		localTime := paths.GetLastTimestampFromFile(sessionLogPath)
   579→		checkpointTime := paths.GetLastTimestampFromBytes(logContent)
   580→		status := strategy.ClassifyTimestamps(localTime, checkpointTime)
   581→
   582→		if status == strategy.StatusLocalNewer {
   583→			sessions := []strategy.SessionRestoreInfo{{
   584→				SessionID:      sessionID,
   585→				Status:         status,
   586→				LocalTime:      localTime,
   587→				CheckpointTime: checkpointTime,
   588→			}}
   589→			shouldOverwrite, promptErr := strategy.PromptOverwriteNewerLogs(sessions)
   590→			if promptErr != nil {
   591→				return fmt.Errorf("failed to get confirmation: %w", promptErr)
   592→			}
   593→			if !shouldOverwrite {
   594→				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Resume cancelled. Local session log preserved.\n")
   595→				return nil
   596→			}
   597→		}
   598→	}
   599→
   600→	// Ensure parent directory exists
   601→	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(sessionLogPath), 0o750); err != nil {
   602→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to create session directory: %w", err)
   603→	}
   604→
   605→	agentSession := &agent.AgentSession{
   606→		SessionID:  sessionID,
   607→		AgentName:  ag.Name(),
   608→		RepoPath:   repoRoot,
   609→		SessionRef: sessionLogPath,
   610→		NativeData: logContent,
   611→	}
   612→
   613→	// Write the session using the agent's WriteSession method
   614→	if err := ag.WriteSession(ctx, agentSession); err != nil {
   615→		logging.Error(ctx, "resume session failed during write",
   616→			slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
   617→			slog.String("session_id", sessionID),
   618→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   619→		)
   620→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to write session: %w", err)
   621→	}
   622→
   623→	logging.Debug(ctx, "resume session completed",
   624→		slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
   625→		slog.String("session_id", sessionID),
   626→	)
   627→
   628→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Session restored to: %s\n", sessionLogPath)
   629→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Session: %s\n", sessionID)
   630→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "\nTo continue this session, run:\n")
   631→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "  %s\n", ag.FormatResumeCommand(sessionID))
   632→
   633→	return nil
   634→}

    82→func runRewindInteractive(ctx context.Context) error { //nolint:maintidx // already present in codebase
    83→	// Get the configured strategy
    84→	start := GetStrategy(ctx)
    85→
    86→	// Check for uncommitted changes first
    87→	canRewind, changeMsg, err := start.CanRewind(ctx)
    88→	if err != nil {
    89→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to check for uncommitted changes: %w", err)
    90→	}
    91→	if !canRewind {
    92→		fmt.Println(changeMsg)
    93→		return nil
    94→	}
    95→
    96→	// Get rewind points from strategy
    97→	points, err := start.GetRewindPoints(ctx, 20)
    98→	if err != nil {
    99→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to find rewind points: %w", err)
   100→	}
   101→
   102→	if len(points) == 0 {
   103→		fmt.Println("No rewind points found.")
   104→		fmt.Println("Rewind points are created automatically when agent sessions end.")
   105→		return nil
   106→	}
   107→
   108→	// Check if there are multiple sessions (to show session identifier)
   109→	sessionIDs := make(map[string]bool)
   110→	for _, p := range points {
   111→		if p.SessionID != "" {
   112→			sessionIDs[p.SessionID] = true
   113→		}
   114→	}
   115→	hasMultipleSessions := len(sessionIDs) > 1
   116→
   117→	// Build options for the select menu
   118→	options := make([]huh.Option[string], 0, len(points)+1)
   119→	for _, p := range points {
   120→		var label string
   121→		timestamp := p.Date.Format("2006-01-02 15:04")
   122→
   123→		// Build session identifier for display when multiple sessions exist
   124→		sessionLabel := ""
   125→		if hasMultipleSessions && p.SessionPrompt != "" {
   126→			// Show truncated prompt to identify the session
   127→			sessionLabel = fmt.Sprintf(" [%s]", sanitizeForTerminal(p.SessionPrompt))
   128→		}
   129→
   130→		switch {
   131→		case p.IsLogsOnly:
   132→			// Committed checkpoint - show commit sha (this is the real user commit)
   133→			shortID := p.ID
   134→			if len(shortID) >= 7 {
   135→				shortID = shortID[:7]
   136→			}
   137→			label = fmt.Sprintf("%s (%s) %s%s", shortID, timestamp, sanitizeForTerminal(p.Message), sessionLabel)
   138→		case p.IsTaskCheckpoint:
   139→			// Task checkpoint (uncommitted) - no sha shown
   140→			label = fmt.Sprintf("        (%s) [Task] %s%s", timestamp, sanitizeForTerminal(p.Message), sessionLabel)
   141→		default:
   142→			// Shadow checkpoint (uncommitted) - no sha shown (internal commit)
   143→			label = fmt.Sprintf("        (%s) %s%s", timestamp, sanitizeForTerminal(p.Message), sessionLabel)
   144→		}
   145→		options = append(options, huh.NewOption(label, p.ID))
   146→	}
   147→	options = append(options, huh.NewOption("Cancel", "cancel"))
   148→
   149→	var selectedID string
   150→	form := NewAccessibleForm(
   151→		huh.NewGroup(
   152→			huh.NewSelect[string]().
   153→				Title("Select a checkpoint to restore").
   154→				Description("Your working directory will be restored to this checkpoint's state").
   155→				Options(options...).
   156→				Value(&selectedID),
   157→		),
   158→	)
   159→
   160→	if err := form.Run(); err != nil {
   161→		return fmt.Errorf("selection cancelled: %w", err)
   162→	}
   163→
   164→	if selectedID == "cancel" {
   165→		fmt.Println("Rewind cancelled.")
   166→		return nil
   167→	}
   168→
   169→	// Find the selected point
   170→	var selectedPoint *strategy.RewindPoint
   171→	for _, p := range points {
   172→		if p.ID == selectedID {
   173→			pointCopy := p
   174→			selectedPoint = &pointCopy
   175→			break
   176→		}
   177→	}
   178→
   179→	if selectedPoint == nil {
   180→		return errors.New("rewind point not found")
   181→	}
   182→
   183→	shortID := selectedPoint.ID
   184→	if len(shortID) > 7 {
   185→		shortID = shortID[:7]
   186→	}
   187→
   188→	// Show what was selected
   189→	switch {
   190→	case selectedPoint.IsLogsOnly:
   191→		// Committed checkpoint - show sha
   192→		fmt.Printf("\nSelected: %s %s\n", shortID, sanitizeForTerminal(selectedPoint.Message))
   193→	case selectedPoint.IsTaskCheckpoint:
   194→		// Task checkpoint - no sha
   195→		fmt.Printf("\nSelected: [Task] %s\n", sanitizeForTerminal(selectedPoint.Message))
   196→	default:
   197→		// Shadow checkpoint - no sha
   198→		fmt.Printf("\nSelected: %s\n", sanitizeForTerminal(selectedPoint.Message))
   199→	}
   200→
   201→	// Handle logs-only points with a sub-choice menu
   202→	if selectedPoint.IsLogsOnly {
   203→		return handleLogsOnlyRewindInteractive(ctx, start, *selectedPoint, shortID)
   204→	}
   205→
   206→	// Preview rewind to show warnings about files that will be deleted
   207→	preview, previewErr := start.PreviewRewind(ctx, *selectedPoint)
   208→	if previewErr == nil && preview != nil && len(preview.FilesToDelete) > 0 {
   209→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "\nWarning: The following untracked files will be DELETED:\n")
   210→		for _, f := range preview.FilesToDelete {
   211→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "  - %s\n", f)
   212→		}
   213→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "\n")
   214→	}
   215→
   216→	// Confirm rewind
   217→	var confirm bool
   218→	description := fmt.Sprintf("This will reset to: %s\nChanges after this point may be lost!", selectedPoint.Message)
   219→	confirmForm := NewAccessibleForm(
   220→		huh.NewGroup(
   221→			huh.NewConfirm().
   222→				Title(fmt.Sprintf("Reset to %s?", shortID)).
   223→				Description(description).
   224→				Value(&confirm),
   225→		),
   226→	)
   227→
   228→	if err := confirmForm.Run(); err != nil {
   229→		return fmt.Errorf("confirmation cancelled: %w", err)
   230→	}
   231→
   232→	if !confirm {
   233→		fmt.Println("Rewind cancelled.")
   234→		return nil
   235→	}
   236→
   237→	// Resolve agent once for use throughout
   238→	agent, err := getAgent(selectedPoint.Agent)
   239→	if err != nil {
   240→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get agent: %w", err)
   241→	}
   242→
   243→	// Initialize logging context with agent from checkpoint
   244→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "rewind")
   245→	logCtx = logging.WithAgent(logCtx, agent.Name())
   246→
   247→	logging.Debug(logCtx, "rewind started",
   248→		slog.String("checkpoint_id", selectedPoint.ID),
   249→		slog.String("session_id", selectedPoint.SessionID),
   250→		slog.Bool("is_task_checkpoint", selectedPoint.IsTaskCheckpoint),
   251→	)
   252→
   253→	// Perform the rewind using strategy
   254→	if err := start.Rewind(ctx, *selectedPoint); err != nil {
   255→		logging.Error(logCtx, "rewind failed",
   256→			slog.String("checkpoint_id", selectedPoint.ID),
   257→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   258→		)
   259→		return err //nolint:wrapcheck // already present in codebase
   260→	}
   261→
   262→	logging.Debug(logCtx, "rewind completed",
   263→		slog.String("checkpoint_id", selectedPoint.ID),
   264→	)
   265→
   266→	// Handle transcript restoration differently for task checkpoints
   267→	var sessionID string
   268→	var transcriptFile string
   269→
   270→	if selectedPoint.IsTaskCheckpoint {
   271→		// For task checkpoint: read checkpoint.json to get UUID and truncate transcript
   272→		checkpoint, err := start.GetTaskCheckpoint(ctx, *selectedPoint)
   273→		if err != nil {
   274→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to read task checkpoint: %v\n", err)
   275→			return nil
   276→		}
   277→
   278→		sessionID = checkpoint.SessionID
   279→
   280→		if checkpoint.CheckpointUUID != "" {
   281→			// Truncate transcript at checkpoint UUID
   282→			if err := restoreTaskCheckpointTranscript(ctx, start, *selectedPoint, sessionID, checkpoint.CheckpointUUID, agent); err != nil {
   283→				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to restore truncated session transcript: %v\n", err)
   284→			} else {
   285→				fmt.Printf("Rewound to task checkpoint. %s\n", agent.FormatResumeCommand(sessionID))
   286→			}
   287→			return nil
   288→		}
   289→	} else {
   290→		// For session checkpoint: restore full transcript
   291→		// Prefer SessionID from trailer (set by GetRewindPoints from Entire-Session trailer)
   292→		// over path-based extraction which is less reliable.
   293→		sessionID = selectedPoint.SessionID
   294→		if sessionID == "" {
   295→			sessionID = filepath.Base(selectedPoint.MetadataDir)
   296→		}
   297→		transcriptFile = filepath.Join(selectedPoint.MetadataDir, paths.TranscriptFileNameLegacy)
   298→	}
   299→
   300→	// Try to restore transcript using the appropriate method:
   301→	// 1. Checkpoint storage (committed checkpoints with valid checkpoint ID)
   302→	// 2. Shadow branch (uncommitted checkpoints with commit hash)
   303→	// 3. Local file (active sessions)
   304→	var restored bool
   305→	if !selectedPoint.CheckpointID.IsEmpty() {
   306→		// Try checkpoint storage first for committed checkpoints
   307→		if returnedSessionID, err := restoreSessionTranscriptFromStrategy(ctx, selectedPoint.CheckpointID, sessionID, agent); err == nil {
   308→			sessionID = returnedSessionID
   309→			restored = true
   310→		}
   311→	}
   312→
   313→	if !restored && selectedPoint.MetadataDir != "" && len(selectedPoint.ID) == 40 {
   314→		// Try shadow branch for uncommitted checkpoints (ID is a 40-char commit hash)
   315→		if returnedSessionID, err := restoreSessionTranscriptFromShadow(ctx, selectedPoint.ID, selectedPoint.MetadataDir, sessionID, agent); err == nil {
   316→			sessionID = returnedSessionID
   317→			restored = true
   318→		}
   319→	}
   320→
   321→	if !restored {
   322→		// Fall back to local file
   323→		if err := restoreSessionTranscript(ctx, transcriptFile, sessionID, agent); err != nil {
   324→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to restore session transcript: %v\n", err)
   325→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "  Source: %s\n", transcriptFile)
   326→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "  Session ID: %s\n", sessionID)
   327→		}
   328→	}
   329→
   330→	fmt.Printf("Rewound to %s. %s\n", shortID, agent.FormatResumeCommand(sessionID))
   331→	return nil
   332→}

   385→func runRewindToInternal(ctx context.Context, commitID string, logsOnly bool, reset bool) error {
   386→	start := GetStrategy(ctx)
   387→
   388→	// Check for uncommitted changes (skip for reset which handles this itself)
   389→	if !reset {
   390→		canRewind, changeMsg, err := start.CanRewind(ctx)
   391→		if err != nil {
   392→			return fmt.Errorf("failed to check for uncommitted changes: %w", err)
   393→		}
   394→		if !canRewind {
   395→			return fmt.Errorf("%s", changeMsg)
   396→		}
   397→	}
   398→
   399→	// Get rewind points
   400→	points, err := start.GetRewindPoints(ctx, 20)
   401→	if err != nil {
   402→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to find rewind points: %w", err)
   403→	}
   404→
   405→	// Find the matching point (support both full and short commit IDs)
   406→	var selectedPoint *strategy.RewindPoint
   407→	for _, p := range points {
   408→		if p.ID == commitID || (len(commitID) >= 7 && len(p.ID) >= 7 && strings.HasPrefix(p.ID, commitID)) {
   409→			pointCopy := p
   410→			selectedPoint = &pointCopy
   411→			break
   412→		}
   413→	}
   414→
   415→	if selectedPoint == nil {
   416→		return fmt.Errorf("rewind point not found: %s", commitID)
   417→	}
   418→
   419→	// Handle reset mode (for logs-only points)
   420→	if reset {
   421→		return handleLogsOnlyResetNonInteractive(ctx, start, *selectedPoint)
   422→	}
   423→
   424→	// Handle logs-only restoration:
   425→	// 1. For logs-only points, always use logs-only restoration
   426→	// 2. If --logs-only flag is set, use logs-only restoration even for checkpoint points
   427→	if selectedPoint.IsLogsOnly || logsOnly {
   428→		return handleLogsOnlyRewindNonInteractive(ctx, start, *selectedPoint)
   429→	}
   430→
   431→	// Preview rewind to show warnings about files that will be deleted
   432→	preview, previewErr := start.PreviewRewind(ctx, *selectedPoint)
   433→	if previewErr == nil && preview != nil && len(preview.FilesToDelete) > 0 {
   434→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "\nWarning: The following untracked files will be DELETED:\n")
   435→		for _, f := range preview.FilesToDelete {
   436→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "  - %s\n", f)
   437→		}
   438→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "\n")
   439→	}
   440→
   441→	// Resolve agent once for use throughout
   442→	agent, err := getAgent(selectedPoint.Agent)
   443→	if err != nil {
   444→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get agent: %w", err)
   445→	}
   446→
   447→	// Initialize logging context with agent from checkpoint
   448→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "rewind")
   449→	logCtx = logging.WithAgent(logCtx, agent.Name())
   450→
   451→	logging.Debug(logCtx, "rewind started",
   452→		slog.String("checkpoint_id", selectedPoint.ID),
   453→		slog.String("session_id", selectedPoint.SessionID),
   454→		slog.Bool("is_task_checkpoint", selectedPoint.IsTaskCheckpoint),
   455→	)
   456→
   457→	// Perform the rewind
   458→	if err := start.Rewind(ctx, *selectedPoint); err != nil {
   459→		logging.Error(logCtx, "rewind failed",
   460→			slog.String("checkpoint_id", selectedPoint.ID),
   461→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   462→		)
   463→		return err //nolint:wrapcheck // already present in codebase
   464→	}
   465→
   466→	logging.Debug(logCtx, "rewind completed",
   467→		slog.String("checkpoint_id", selectedPoint.ID),
   468→	)
   469→
   470→	// Handle transcript restoration
   471→	var sessionID string
   472→	var transcriptFile string
   473→
   474→	if selectedPoint.IsTaskCheckpoint {
   475→		checkpoint, err := start.GetTaskCheckpoint(ctx, *selectedPoint)
   476→		if err != nil {
   477→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to read task checkpoint: %v\n", err)
   478→			return nil
   479→		}
   480→
   481→		sessionID = checkpoint.SessionID
   482→
   483→		if checkpoint.CheckpointUUID != "" {
   484→			// Use strategy-based transcript restoration for task checkpoints
   485→			if err := restoreTaskCheckpointTranscript(ctx, start, *selectedPoint, sessionID, checkpoint.CheckpointUUID, agent); err != nil {
   486→				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to restore truncated session transcript: %v\n", err)
   487→			} else {
   488→				fmt.Printf("Rewound to task checkpoint. %s\n", agent.FormatResumeCommand(sessionID))
   489→			}
   490→			return nil
   491→		}
   492→	} else {
   493→		// Prefer SessionID from trailer over path-based extraction
   494→		sessionID = selectedPoint.SessionID
   495→		if sessionID == "" {
   496→			sessionID = filepath.Base(selectedPoint.MetadataDir)
   497→		}
   498→		transcriptFile = filepath.Join(selectedPoint.MetadataDir, paths.TranscriptFileNameLegacy)
   499→	}
   500→
   501→	// Try to restore transcript using the appropriate method:
   502→	// 1. Checkpoint storage (committed checkpoints with valid checkpoint ID)
   503→	// 2. Shadow branch (uncommitted checkpoints with commit hash)
   504→	// 3. Local file (active sessions)
   505→	var restored bool
   506→	if !selectedPoint.CheckpointID.IsEmpty() {
   507→		// Try checkpoint storage first for committed checkpoints
   508→		if returnedSessionID, err := restoreSessionTranscriptFromStrategy(ctx, selectedPoint.CheckpointID, sessionID, agent); err == nil {
   509→			sessionID = returnedSessionID
   510→			restored = true
   511→		}
   512→	}
   513→
   514→	if !restored && selectedPoint.MetadataDir != "" && len(selectedPoint.ID) == 40 {
   515→		// Try shadow branch for uncommitted checkpoints (ID is a 40-char commit hash)
   516→		if returnedSessionID, err := restoreSessionTranscriptFromShadow(ctx, selectedPoint.ID, selectedPoint.MetadataDir, sessionID, agent); err == nil {
   517→			sessionID = returnedSessionID
   518→			restored = true
   519→		}
   520→	}
   521→
   522→	if !restored {
   523→		// Fall back to local file
   524→		if err := restoreSessionTranscript(ctx, transcriptFile, sessionID, agent); err != nil {
   525→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to restore session transcript: %v\n", err)
   526→		}
   527→	}
   528→
   529→	fmt.Printf("Rewound to %s. %s\n", selectedPoint.ID[:7], agent.FormatResumeCommand(sessionID))
   530→	return nil
   531→}

   533→// handleLogsOnlyRewindNonInteractive handles logs-only rewind in non-interactive mode.
   534→// Defaults to restoring logs only (no checkout) for safety.
   535→func handleLogsOnlyRewindNonInteractive(ctx context.Context, start *strategy.ManualCommitStrategy, point strategy.RewindPoint) error {
   536→	// Resolve agent once for use throughout
   537→	agent, err := getAgent(point.Agent)
   538→	if err != nil {
   539→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get agent: %w", err)
   540→	}
   541→
   542→	// Initialize logging context with agent from checkpoint
   543→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "rewind")
   544→	logCtx = logging.WithAgent(logCtx, agent.Name())
   545→
   546→	logging.Debug(logCtx, "logs-only rewind started",

   548→		slog.String("session_id", point.SessionID),
   549→	)
   550→
   551→	sessions, err := start.RestoreLogsOnly(ctx, point, true) // force=true for explicit rewind
   552→	if err != nil {

   554→			slog.String("checkpoint_id", point.ID),
   555→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   556→		)
   557→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to restore logs: %w", err)
   558→	}
   559→
   560→	logging.Debug(logCtx, "logs-only rewind completed",

   562→	)
   563→
   564→	// Show resume commands for all sessions
   565→	printMultiSessionResumeCommands(sessions)
   566→
   567→	fmt.Println("Note: Working directory unchanged. Use interactive mode for full checkout.")
   568→	return nil
   569→}

   571→// handleLogsOnlyResetNonInteractive handles reset in non-interactive mode.
   572→// This performs a git reset --hard to the target commit.
   573→func handleLogsOnlyResetNonInteractive(ctx context.Context, start *strategy.ManualCommitStrategy, point strategy.RewindPoint) error {
   574→	// Resolve agent once for use throughout
   575→	agent, err := getAgent(point.Agent)
   576→	if err != nil {

   578→	}
   579→
   580→	// Initialize logging context with agent from checkpoint
   581→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "rewind")

   585→		slog.String("checkpoint_id", point.ID),
   586→		slog.String("session_id", point.SessionID),
   587→	)
   588→
   589→	// Get current HEAD before reset (for recovery message)
   590→	currentHead, headErr := getCurrentHeadHash(ctx)
   591→	if headErr != nil {
   592→		currentHead = ""
   593→	}
   594→
   595→	// Restore logs first
   596→	sessions, err := start.RestoreLogsOnly(ctx, point, true) // force=true for explicit rewind
   597→	if err != nil {

   599→			slog.String("checkpoint_id", point.ID),
   600→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   601→		)
   602→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to restore logs: %w", err)
   603→	}
   604→
   605→	// Perform git reset --hard
   606→	if err := performGitResetHard(ctx, point.ID); err != nil {
   607→		logging.Error(logCtx, "logs-only reset failed during git reset",
   608→			slog.String("checkpoint_id", point.ID),
   609→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   610→		)
   611→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to reset branch: %w", err)
   612→	}
   613→
   614→	logging.Debug(logCtx, "logs-only reset completed",
   615→		slog.String("checkpoint_id", point.ID),
   616→	)
   617→
   618→	shortID := point.ID
   619→	if len(shortID) > 7 {
   620→		shortID = shortID[:7]
   621→	}
   622→
   623→	fmt.Printf("Reset branch to %s.\n", shortID)
   624→
   625→	// Show resume commands for all sessions
   626→	printMultiSessionResumeCommands(sessions)
   627→
   628→	// Show recovery instructions
   629→	if currentHead != "" && currentHead != point.ID {
   630→		currentShort := currentHead
   631→		if len(currentShort) > 7 {
   632→			currentShort = currentShort[:7]
   633→		}
   634→		fmt.Printf("\nTo undo this reset: git reset --hard %s\n", currentShort)
   635→	}
   636→
   637→	return nil
   638→}

  1023→// getCurrentHeadHash returns the current HEAD commit hash.
  1024→func getCurrentHeadHash(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
  1025→	repo, err := openRepository(ctx)
  1026→	if err != nil {
  1027→		return "", err
  1028→	}
  1029→
  1030→	head, err := repo.Head()
  1031→	if err != nil {
  1032→		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to get HEAD: %w", err)
  1033→	}
  1034→
  1035→	return head.Hash().String(), nil
  1036→}

  1038→// checkResetSafety checks for potential issues before a git reset --hard.
  1039→// Returns a list of warning messages (empty if safe to proceed without warnings).
  1040→// If uncommittedChangesWarning is provided, it will be used instead of a generic warning.
  1041→func checkResetSafety(ctx context.Context, targetCommitHash string, uncommittedChangesWarning string) ([]string, error) {
  1042→	var warnings []string
  1043→
  1044→	repo, err := openRepository(ctx)
  1045→	if err != nil {
  1046→		return nil, err
  1047→	}
  1048→
  1049→	// Check for uncommitted changes
  1050→	if uncommittedChangesWarning != "" {
  1051→		// Use the detailed warning from strategy's CanRewind()
  1052→		warnings = append(warnings, uncommittedChangesWarning)
  1053→	} else {
  1054→		// Fall back to generic check
  1055→		worktree, err := repo.Worktree()
  1056→		if err != nil {
  1057→			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get worktree: %w", err)
  1058→		}
  1059→
  1060→		status, err := worktree.Status()
  1061→		if err != nil {
  1062→			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get status: %w", err)
  1063→		}
  1064→
  1065→		if !status.IsClean() {
  1066→			warnings = append(warnings, "• You have uncommitted changes that will be LOST")
  1067→		}
  1068→	}
  1069→
  1070→	// Check if current HEAD is ahead of target (we'd be discarding commits)
  1071→	head, err := repo.Head()
  1072→	if err != nil {
  1073→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get HEAD: %w", err)
  1074→	}
  1075→
  1076→	targetHash := plumbing.NewHash(targetCommitHash)
  1077→
  1078→	// Count commits between target and HEAD
  1079→	commitsAhead, err := countCommitsBetween(repo, targetHash, head.Hash())
  1080→	if err != nil {
  1081→		// Non-fatal - just can't show commit count
  1082→		commitsAhead = -1
  1083→	}
  1084→
  1085→	if commitsAhead > 0 {
  1086→		warnings = append(warnings, fmt.Sprintf("• %d commit(s) after this point will be orphaned", commitsAhead))
  1087→	}
  1088→
  1089→	return warnings, nil
  1090→}

  1092→// countCommitsBetween counts commits between ancestor and descendant.
  1093→// Returns 0 if ancestor == descendant, -1 on error.
  1094→func countCommitsBetween(repo *git.Repository, ancestor, descendant plumbing.Hash) (int, error) {
  1095→	if ancestor == descendant {
  1096→		return 0, nil
  1097→	}
  1098→
  1099→	// Walk from descendant back to ancestor
  1100→	count := 0
  1101→	current := descendant
  1102→
  1103→	for count < strategy.MaxCommitTraversalDepth { // Safety limit
  1104→		if current == ancestor {
  1105→			return count, nil
  1106→		}
  1107→
  1108→		commit, err := repo.CommitObject(current)
  1109→		if err != nil {
  1110→			return -1, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit: %w", err)
  1111→		}
  1112→
  1113→		if commit.NumParents() == 0 {
  1114→			// Reached root without finding ancestor - ancestor not in history
  1115→			return -1, nil
  1116→		}
  1117→
  1118→		count++
  1119→		current = commit.ParentHashes[0] // Follow first parent
  1120→	}
  1121→
  1122→	return -1, nil
  1123→}

  1139→// sanitizeForTerminal removes or replaces characters that cause rendering issues
  1140→// in terminal UI components. This includes emojis with skin-tone modifiers and
  1141→// other multi-codepoint characters that confuse width calculations.
  1142→func sanitizeForTerminal(s string) string {
  1143→	var result strings.Builder
  1144→	result.Grow(len(s))
  1145→
  1146→	for _, r := range s {
  1147→		// Skip emoji skin tone modifiers (U+1F3FB to U+1F3FF)
  1148→		if r >= 0x1F3FB && r <= 0x1F3FF {
  1149→			continue
  1150→		}
  1151→		// Skip zero-width joiners used in emoji sequences
  1152→		if r == 0x200D {
  1153→			continue
  1154→		}
  1155→		// Skip variation selectors (U+FE00 to U+FE0F)
  1156→		if r >= 0xFE00 && r <= 0xFE0F {
  1157→			continue
  1158→		}
  1159→		// Keep printable characters and common whitespace
  1160→		if unicode.IsPrint(r) || r == '\t' || r == '\n' {
  1161→			result.WriteRune(r)
  1162→		}
  1163→	}
  1164→
  1165→	return result.String()
  1166→}

    16→	// MetadataTrailerKey points to the metadata directory within a commit tree.
    17→	MetadataTrailerKey = "Entire-Metadata"
    18→
    19→	// MetadataTaskTrailerKey points to the task metadata directory for subagent checkpoints.
    20→	MetadataTaskTrailerKey = "Entire-Metadata-Task"

    22→	// StrategyTrailerKey indicates which strategy created the commit.

    25→	// BaseCommitTrailerKey links shadow commits to their base code commit.

    28→	// SessionTrailerKey identifies which session created a commit.

    30→
    31→	// CondensationTrailerKey identifies the condensation ID for a commit (legacy).
    32→	CondensationTrailerKey = "Entire-Condensation"

    34→	// SourceRefTrailerKey links code commits to their metadata on a shadow/metadata branch.

    38→	// CheckpointTrailerKey links commits to their checkpoint metadata on entire/checkpoints/v1.
    39→	// Format: 12 hex characters e.g. "a3b2c4d5e6f7"
    40→	// This trailer survives git amend and rebase operations.
    41→	CheckpointTrailerKey = "Entire-Checkpoint"

    43→	// EphemeralBranchTrailerKey identifies the shadow branch that a checkpoint originated from.
    44→	// Used in manual-commit strategy checkpoint commits on entire/checkpoints/v1 branch.

    48→	// AgentTrailerKey identifies the agent that created a checkpoint.

    53→// Pre-compiled regexes for trailer parsing.

   127→// ParseCheckpoint extracts the checkpoint ID from a commit message.
   128→// Returns the CheckpointID and true if found, empty ID and false otherwise.
   129→func ParseCheckpoint(commitMessage string) (checkpointID.CheckpointID, bool) {
   130→	matches := checkpointTrailerRegex.FindStringSubmatch(commitMessage)
   131→	if len(matches) > 1 {
   132→		idStr := strings.TrimSpace(matches[1])
   133→		// Validate it's a proper checkpoint ID
   134→		if cpID, err := checkpointID.NewCheckpointID(idStr); err == nil {

   141→// ParseAllCheckpoints extracts all checkpoint IDs from a commit message.
   142→// Returns a slice of CheckpointIDs (may be empty if none found).
   143→// Duplicate IDs are deduplicated while preserving order.
   144→// This is useful for squash merge commits that contain multiple Entire-Checkpoint trailers.
   145→func ParseAllCheckpoints(commitMessage string) []checkpointID.CheckpointID {
   146→	matches := checkpointTrailerRegex.FindAllStringSubmatch(commitMessage, -1)
   147→	if len(matches) == 0 {
   148→		return nil
   149→	}
   150→
   151→	seen := make(map[string]bool)
   152→	ids := make([]checkpointID.CheckpointID, 0, len(matches))
   153→	for _, match := range matches {
   154→		if len(match) > 1 {
   155→			idStr := strings.TrimSpace(match[1])
   156→			if !seen[idStr] {
   157→				if cpID, err := checkpointID.NewCheckpointID(idStr); err == nil {
   158→					seen[idStr] = true
   159→					ids = append(ids, cpID)
   160→				}
   161→			}
   162→		}
   163→	}
   164→	return ids
   165→}

**`findBranchCheckpoints()`** (line 268) works as follows:

Now here are the two UX options for rewind:

---

### Option A: Match `entire resume` behavior — auto-resolve to latest

The squash merge commit appears as **one entry** in the rewind list (like today), but it restores the **latest** checkpoint instead of the first one found. The user sees:

```
? Select a rewind point:
  > [1h ago] Committed: abc1234 — "Add auth system (#42)"  (logs only, 3 checkpoints)
```

After selecting it, the existing logs-only sub-menu appears. The CLI restores the latest checkpoint's transcript and prints:

```
Found 3 checkpoints in squash commit abc1234, restoring from the latest (2 older skipped)
Restored session: 2026-03-04-session-3
Resume with: claude -r 2026-03-04-session-3
```

**Pros:**
- Consistent with `entire resume` behavior
- Simple — no extra interaction step
- Usually what you want (the latest checkpoint has the most context)

**Cons:**
- Older checkpoints from the squash are still inaccessible — if you specifically wanted checkpoint 1 of 3, you can't get it
- The "(3 checkpoints)" label hints at data the user can't actually reach

### Option B: Expand into separate rewind points per checkpoint

Each checkpoint in the squash merge gets its own entry in the rewind list:

    [1h ago] Committed: abc1234 — "Add auth model" (1/3)           (logs only)

Each entry has its own `CheckpointID` and maps to a distinct set of session transcripts on `entire/checkpoints/v1`. Selecting any one of them goes through the normal logs-only sub-menu and restores that specific checkpoint's data.

- Full access to all checkpoint data — nothing is silently lost
- User can pick exactly which point in the squash they want
- Each checkpoint may have different sessions/transcripts, and the user can see that

**Cons:**
- Squash merges with many commits could bloat the list (10 commits = 10 entries from one squash)
- Slightly inconsistent with `entire resume` (which auto-picks latest)
- The entries share the same commit hash, which could look odd

---

### My take

**Option A is the right call.** Here's why:

1. **Consistency matters.** `entire resume` already established the pattern: squash merge → resolve to latest. Users who learn one command won't be surprised by the other.

2. **Rewind's purpose for logs-only points is transcript restoration.** You're not restoring files (the squash commit is already on the branch). The latest checkpoint's transcript is almost always the one you want — it has the full conversation context up to that point.

3. **Option B's benefit is theoretical.** In practice, if someone squash-merged 3 commits, they almost certainly want to resume from where they left off (the latest), not from checkpoint 1 of 3 where the agent had barely started. 4. **The fix is minimal.** Swap `ParseCheckpoint` for `ParseAllCheckpoints` + `resolveLatestCheckpoint()` (or a shared helper), and you're done. The existing `RestoreLogsOnly()` already handles multi-session checkpoints correctly downstream.

# Brainstorming Ideas Into Designs

## Overview

Help turn ideas into fully formed designs and specs through natural collaborative dialogue.

Start by understanding the current project context, then ask questions one at a time to refine the idea. Once you understand what you're building, present the design and get user approval.

<HARD-GATE>
Do NOT invoke any implementation skill, write any code, scaffold any project, or take any implementation action until you have presented a design and the user has approved it. This applies to EVERY project regardless of perceived simplicity.
</HARD-GATE>

## Anti-Pattern: "This Is Too Simple To Need A Design"

Every project goes through this process. A todo list, a single-function utility, a config change — all of them. "Simple" projects are where unexamined assumptions cause the most wasted work. The design can be short (a few sentences for truly simple projects), but you MUST present it and get approval.

## Checklist

You MUST create a task for each of these items and complete them in order:

1. **Explore project context** — check files, docs, recent commits
2. **Ask clarifying questions** — one at a time, understand purpose/constraints/success criteria
3. **Propose 2-3 approaches** — with trade-offs and your recommendation
4. **Present design** — in sections scaled to their complexity, get user approval after each section
5. **Write design doc** — save to `docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md` and commit
6. **Transition to implementation** — invoke writing-plans skill to create implementation plan

## Process Flow

```dot
digraph brainstorming {
    "Explore project context" [shape=box];
    "Ask clarifying questions" [shape=box];
    "Propose 2-3 approaches" [shape=box];
    "Present design sections" [shape=box];
    "User approves design?" [shape=diamond];
    "Write design doc" [shape=box];
    "Invoke writing-plans skill" [shape=doublecircle];

    "Explore project context" -> "Ask clarifying questions";
    "Ask clarifying questions" -> "Propose 2-3 approaches";
    "Propose 2-3 approaches" -> "Present design sections";
    "Present design sections" -> "User approves design?";
    "User approves design?" -> "Present design sections" [label="no, revise"];
    "User approves design?" -> "Write design doc" [label="yes"];
    "Write design doc" -> "Invoke writing-plans skill";
}
```

**The terminal state is invoking writing-plans.** Do NOT invoke frontend-design, mcp-builder, or any other implementation skill. The ONLY skill you invoke after brainstorming is writing-plans.

## The Process

**Understanding the idea:**

- Ask after each section whether it looks right so far
- Cover: architecture, components, data flow, error handling, testing
- Be ready to go back and clarify if something doesn't make sense

**Documentation:**
- Write the validated design to `docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`

- **Explore alternatives** - Always propose 2-3 approaches before settling
- **Incremental validation** - Present design, get approval before moving on
- **Be flexible** - Go back and clarify when something doesn't make sense

Base directory for this skill: /Users/pfleidi/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/superpowers/4.3.1/skills/test-driven-development

# Test-Driven Development (TDD)

## Overview

Write the test first. Watch it fail. Write minimal code to pass.

**Core principle:** If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing.

**Violating the letter of the rules is violating the spirit of the rules.**

## When to Use

**Always:**
- New features
- Bug fixes
- Refactoring
- Behavior changes

**Exceptions (ask your human partner):**
- Throwaway prototypes
- Generated code
- Configuration files

Thinking "skip TDD just this once"? Stop. That's rationalization.

## The Iron Law

```
NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST
```

Write code before the test? Delete it. Start over.

**No exceptions:**
- Don't keep it as "reference"
- Don't "adapt" it while writing tests
- Don't look at it
- Delete means delete

Implement fresh from tests. Period.

## Red-Green-Refactor

```dot
digraph tdd_cycle {
    rankdir=LR;
    red [label="RED\nWrite failing test", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ffcccc"];
    verify_red [label="Verify fails\ncorrectly", shape=diamond];
    green [label="GREEN\nMinimal code", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccffcc"];
    verify_green [label="Verify passes\nAll green", shape=diamond];
    refactor [label="REFACTOR\nClean up", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccccff"];
    next [label="Next", shape=ellipse];

    red -> verify_red;
    verify_red -> green [label="yes"];
    verify_red -> red [label="wrong\nfailure"];
    green -> verify_green;
    verify_green -> refactor [label="yes"];
    verify_green -> green [label="no"];
    refactor -> verify_green [label="stay\ngreen"];
    verify_green -> next;
    next -> red;
}
```

### RED - Write Failing Test

Write one minimal test showing what should happen.

<Good>
```typescript
test('retries failed operations 3 times', async () => {
  let attempts = 0;
  const operation = () => {
    attempts++;
    if (attempts < 3) throw new Error('fail');
    return 'success';
  };

  const result = await retryOperation(operation);

  expect(result).toBe('success');
  expect(attempts).toBe(3);
});
```
Clear name, tests real behavior, one thing
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
test('retry works', async () => {
  const mock = jest.fn()
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockResolvedValueOnce('success');
  await retryOperation(mock);
  expect(mock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
});
```
Vague name, tests mock not code
</Bad>

**Requirements:**
- One behavior
- Clear name
- Real code (no mocks unless unavoidable)

### Verify RED - Watch It Fail

**MANDATORY. Never skip.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test fails (not errors)
- Failure message is expected
- Fails because feature missing (not typos)

**Test passes?** You're testing existing behavior. Fix test.

**Test errors?** Fix error, re-run until it fails correctly.

### GREEN - Minimal Code

Write simplest code to pass the test.

<Good>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    try {
      return await fn();
    } catch (e) {
      if (i === 2) throw e;
    }
  }
  throw new Error('unreachable');
}
```
Just enough to pass
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(
  fn: () => Promise<T>,
  options?: {
    maxRetries?: number;
    backoff?: 'linear' | 'exponential';
    onRetry?: (attempt: number) => void;
  }
): Promise<T> {
  // YAGNI
}
```
Over-engineered
</Bad>

Don't add features, refactor other code, or "improve" beyond the test.

### Verify GREEN - Watch It Pass

**MANDATORY.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test passes
- Other tests still pass
- Output pristine (no errors, warnings)

**Test fails?** Fix code, not test.

**Other tests fail?** Fix now.

### REFACTOR - Clean Up

After green only:
- Remove duplication
- Improve names
- Extract helpers

Keep tests green. Don't add behavior.

### Repeat

Next failing test for next feature.

## Good Tests

| Quality | Good | Bad |
|---------|------|-----|
| **Minimal** | One thing. "and" in name? Split it. | `test('validates email and domain and whitespace')` |
| **Clear** | Name describes behavior | `test('test1')` |
| **Shows intent** | Demonstrates desired API | Obscures what code should do |

## Why Order Matters

**"I'll write tests after to verify it works"**

Tests written after code pass immediately. Passing immediately proves nothing:
- Might test wrong thing
- Might test implementation, not behavior
- Might miss edge cases you forgot
- You never saw it catch the bug

Test-first forces you to see the test fail, proving it actually tests something.

**"I already manually tested all the edge cases"**

Manual testing is ad-hoc. You think you tested everything but:
- No record of what you tested
- Can't re-run when code changes
- Easy to forget cases under pressure
- "It worked when I tried it" ≠ comprehensive

Automated tests are systematic. They run the same way every time.

**"Deleting X hours of work is wasteful"**

Sunk cost fallacy. The time is already gone. Your choice now:
- Delete and rewrite with TDD (X more hours, high confidence)
- Keep it and add tests after (30 min, low confidence, likely bugs)

The "waste" is keeping code you can't trust. Working code without real tests is technical debt.

**"TDD is dogmatic, being pragmatic means adapting"**

TDD IS pragmatic:
- Finds bugs before commit (faster than debugging after)
- Prevents regressions (tests catch breaks immediately)
- Documents behavior (tests show how to use code)
- Enables refactoring (change freely, tests catch breaks)

"Pragmatic" shortcuts = debugging in production = slower.

**"Tests after achieve the same goals - it's spirit not ritual"**

No. Tests-after answer "What does this do?" Tests-first answer "What should this do?"

Tests-after are biased by your implementation. You test what you built, not what's required. You verify remembered edge cases, not discovered ones.

Tests-first force edge case discovery before implementing. Tests-after verify you remembered everything (you didn't).

30 minutes of tests after ≠ TDD. You get coverage, lose proof tests work.

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Too simple to test" | Simple code breaks. Test takes 30 seconds. |
| "I'll test after" | Tests passing immediately prove nothing. |
| "Tests after achieve same goals" | Tests-after = "what does this do?" Tests-first = "what should this do?" |
| "Already manually tested" | Ad-hoc ≠ systematic. No record, can't re-run. |
| "Deleting X hours is wasteful" | Sunk cost fallacy. Keeping unverified code is technical debt. |
| "Keep as reference, write tests first" | You'll adapt it. That's testing after. Delete means delete. |
| "Need to explore first" | Fine. Throw away exploration, start with TDD. |
| "Test hard = design unclear" | Listen to test. Hard to test = hard to use. |
| "TDD will slow me down" | TDD faster than debugging. Pragmatic = test-first. |
| "Manual test faster" | Manual doesn't prove edge cases. You'll re-test every change. |
| "Existing code has no tests" | You're improving it. Add tests for existing code. |

## Red Flags - STOP and Start Over

- Code before test
- Test after implementation
- Test passes immediately
- Can't explain why test failed
- Tests added "later"
- Rationalizing "just this once"
- "I already manually tested it"
- "Tests after achieve the same purpose"
- "It's about spirit not ritual"
- "Keep as reference" or "adapt existing code"
- "Already spent X hours, deleting is wasteful"
- "TDD is dogmatic, I'm being pragmatic"
- "This is different because..."

**All of these mean: Delete code. Start over with TDD.**

## Example: Bug Fix

**Bug:** Empty email accepted

**RED**
```typescript
test('rejects empty email', async () => {
  const result = await submitForm({ email: '' });
  expect(result.error).toBe('Email required');
});
```

**Verify RED**
```bash
$ npm test
FAIL: expected 'Email required', got undefined
```

**GREEN**
```typescript
function submitForm(data: FormData) {
  if (!data.email?.trim()) {
    return { error: 'Email required' };
  }
  // ...
}
```

**Verify GREEN**
```bash
$ npm test
PASS
```

**REFACTOR**
Extract validation for multiple fields if needed.

## Verification Checklist

Before marking work complete:

- [ ] Every new function/method has a test
- [ ] Watched each test fail before implementing
- [ ] Each test failed for expected reason (feature missing, not typo)
- [ ] Wrote minimal code to pass each test
- [ ] All tests pass
- [ ] Output pristine (no errors, warnings)
- [ ] Tests use real code (mocks only if unavoidable)
- [ ] Edge cases and errors covered

Can't check all boxes? You skipped TDD. Start over.

## When Stuck

| Problem | Solution |
|---------|----------|
| Don't know how to test | Write wished-for API. Write assertion first. Ask your human partner. |
| Test too complicated | Design too complicated. Simplify interface. |
| Must mock everything | Code too coupled. Use dependency injection. |
| Test setup huge | Extract helpers. Still complex? Simplify design. |

## Debugging Integration

Bug found? Write failing test reproducing it. Follow TDD cycle. Test proves fix and prevents regression.

Never fix bugs without a test.

## Testing Anti-Patterns

When adding mocks or test utilities, read @testing-anti-patterns.md to avoid common pitfalls:
- Testing mock behavior instead of real behavior
- Adding test-only methods to production classes
- Mocking without understanding dependencies

## Final Rule

```
Production code → test exists and failed first
Otherwise → not TDD
```

No exceptions without your human partner's permission.

content.text:
All tests pass, lint is clean.

Regarding your question — yes, they're similar but have different signatures. `resolveLatestCheckpoint` (resume.go) takes `[]id.CheckpointID` and fetches the metadata tree itself (with remote fallback), returning `(id.CheckpointID, *object.Tree, error)`. My `resolveLatestCheckpointFromMap` takes a pre-built info map and an already-fetched tree, returning `(id.CheckpointID, CheckpointInfo, bool)`.

The core sorting logic is the same: read metadata, sort by `CreatedAt`, pick the last. Let me refactor to extract a shared helper in the strategy package that both can use.

`collectCheckpointsByAge` in resume.go is the shared kernel. It reads metadata from the tree and sorts by age. I can move it to the strategy package (since it only depends on `strategy.ReadCheckpointMetadata` and `strategy.CheckpointInfo`), then have both resume.go and `resolveLatestCheckpointFromMap` use it.

Let me do that refactoring.

# Requesting Code Review

Dispatch superpowers:code-reviewer subagent to catch issues before they cascade.

**Core principle:** Review early, review often.

## When to Request Review

**Mandatory:**
- After each task in subagent-driven development
- After completing major feature
- Before merge to main

**Optional but valuable:**
- When stuck (fresh perspective)
- Before refactoring (baseline check)
- After fixing complex bug

## How to Request

**1. Get git SHAs:**
```bash
BASE_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD~1)  # or origin/main
HEAD_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
```

**2. Dispatch code-reviewer subagent:**

Use Task tool with superpowers:code-reviewer type, fill template at `code-reviewer.md`

**Placeholders:**
- `{WHAT_WAS_IMPLEMENTED}` - What you just built
- `{PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS}` - What it should do
- `{BASE_SHA}` - Starting commit
- `{HEAD_SHA}` - Ending commit
- `{DESCRIPTION}` - Brief summary

**3. Act on feedback:**
- Fix Critical issues immediately
- Fix Important issues before proceeding
- Note Minor issues for later
- Push back if reviewer is wrong (with reasoning)

## Example

```
[Just completed Task 2: Add verification function]

You: Let me request code review before proceeding.

BASE_SHA=$(git log --oneline | grep "Task 1" | head -1 | awk '{print review}')
HEAD_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)

[Dispatch superpowers:code-reviewer subagent]
  WHAT_WAS_IMPLEMENTED: Verification and repair functions for conversation index
  PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS: Task 2 from docs/plans/deployment-plan.md
  BASE_SHA: a7981ec
  HEAD_SHA: 3df7661
  DESCRIPTION: Added verifyIndex() and repairIndex() with 4 issue types

[Subagent returns]:
  Strengths: Clean architecture, real tests
  Issues:
    Important: Missing progress indicators
    Minor: Magic number (100) for reporting interval
  Assessment: Ready to proceed

You: [Fix progress indicators]
[Continue to Task 3]
```

## Integration with Workflows

**Subagent-Driven Development:**
- Review after EACH task
- Catch issues before they compound
- Fix before moving to next task

**Executing Plans:**
- Review after each batch (3 tasks)
- Get feedback, apply, continue

**Ad-Hoc Development:**
- Review before merge
- Review when stuck

## Red Flags

**Never:**
- Skip review because "it's simple"
- Ignore Critical issues
- Proceed with unfixed Important issues
- Argue with valid technical feedback

**If reviewer wrong:**
- Push back with technical reasoning
- Show code/tests that prove it works
- Request clarification

See template at: requesting-code-review/code-reviewer.md

## Code Review: Fix Squash Merge Rewind

### Overall Assessment

This is a clean, well-scoped fix. The implementation correctly addresses the bug where `entire rewind` only parsed the first `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer from squash merge commits, and it achieves consistency with `entire resume` by reusing the same resolution logic. All tests pass. Linting is clean.

### What Was Done Well

- **Correct root cause fix.** Switching from `ParseCheckpoint` (single match) to `ParseAllCheckpoints` (all matches) in `/Users/pfleidi/entire/cli/.worktrees/fix-squash-merge-rewind/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_rewind.go` directly addresses the bug.
- **Shared helper extraction.** `CollectCheckpointsByAge` in `/Users/pfleidi/entire/cli/.worktrees/fix-squash-merge-rewind/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/common.go` avoids duplicating the sort-by-creation-time logic between resume and rewind.
- **Backward-compatible wrapper.** The local `collectCheckpointsByAge` in `/Users/pfleidi/entire/cli/.worktrees/fix-squash-merge-rewind/cmd/entire/cli/resume.go` delegates to the new shared helper, keeping the call sites unchanged.
- **Thorough integration test.** `REDACTED` in `/Users/pfleidi/entire/cli/.worktrees/fix-squash-merge-rewind/cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/logs_only_rewind_test.go` covers the full scenario: two sessions, two commits, squash merge, and verification that the latest checkpoint is used.
- **Defensive fallback.** `resolveLatestCheckpointFromMap` has a fallback path using the info map's `CreatedAt` when `metadataTree` is nil, which handles edge cases gracefully.

### Plan Alignment

The implementation matches the stated requirements precisely:
- Multiple `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers are now parsed.
- Resolution picks the latest checkpoint by creation time.
- Behavior is consistent with `entire resume`.
- Shared `CollectCheckpointsByAge` deduplicates logic between resume and rewind.

### Issues

**Important (should fix):**

1. **Double metadata read in the multi-checkpoint path.** In `resolveLatestCheckpointFromMap` at `/Users/pfleidi/entire/cli/.worktrees/fix-squash-merge-rewind/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_rewind.go` lines 274-283, when there are multiple valid IDs, `CollectCheckpointsByAge` calls `ReadCheckpointMetadata` for each checkpoint ID. However, these same checkpoint IDs already have their metadata loaded in `checkpointInfoMap` (built at lines 155-160 of the same file from `listCheckpoints`). The `CollectCheckpointsByAge` call re-reads metadata from the tree unnecessarily. The fallback path (lines 285-292) already does the right thing -- it uses the in-memory map. For multi-checkpoint squash merges, the fallback logic is sufficient and avoids redundant tree I/O.

   Specifically, the `CollectCheckpointsByAge` call reads `CreatedAt` from tree blobs, but `checkpointInfoMap` already contains `CheckpointInfo` structs with `CreatedAt` populated. The fallback loop does the same comparison using `infoMap[cpID].CreatedAt`. Unless the tree metadata and the in-memory metadata could have different `CreatedAt` values (which would be a separate bug), the `CollectCheckpointsByAge` code path is redundant.

   Recommendation: Consider removing the `CollectCheckpointsByAge` call from `resolveLatestCheckpointFromMap` and using only the in-memory fallback logic. This simplifies the function and avoids extra tree reads:

   ```go
   func resolveLatestCheckpointFromMap(cpIDs []id.CheckpointID, infoMap map[id.CheckpointID]CheckpointInfo, _ *object.Tree) (CheckpointInfo, bool) {
       var validIDs []id.CheckpointID
       for _, cpID := range cpIDs {
           if _, ok := infoMap[cpID]; ok {
               validIDs = append(validIDs, cpID)
           }
       }
       if len(validIDs) == 0 {
           return CheckpointInfo{}, false
       }
       info := infoMap[validIDs[0]]
       for _, cpID := range validIDs[1:] {
           if candidate := infoMap[cpID]; candidate.CreatedAt.After(info.CreatedAt) {
               info = candidate
           }
       }
       return info, true
   }
   ```

   If there is a reason the tree metadata could differ from the in-memory metadata, that should be documented with a comment.

**Suggestions (nice to have):**

2. **The `collectCheckpointsByAge` wrapper in resume.go is now trivial.** After the refactoring, the wrapper at `/Users/pfleidi/entire/cli/.worktrees/fix-squash-merge-rewind/cmd/entire/cli/resume.go` lines 237-241 is a single-line delegation. The comment says it is "kept as a local wrapper for call-site brevity," but there is only one call site (line 206). Inlining `strategy.CollectCheckpointsByAge(metadataTree, checkpointIDs)` directly would reduce indirection. This is minor and not blocking.

3. **Test could verify which checkpoint's transcript is restored.** The test at `/Users/pfleidi/entire/cli/.worktrees/fix-squash-merge-rewind/cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/logs_only_rewind_test.go` lines 556-575 verifies that *a* transcript `.jsonl` file exists after logs-only rewind, but does not verify that the content corresponds to session 2 (the latest checkpoint). Since the core assertion is that the *latest* checkpoint is chosen, verifying the restored transcript content would strengthen the test. For example, reading the `.jsonl` file and checking it contains "goodbye" rather than "hello" would confirm end-to-end correctness.

4. **Type asymmetry between `CollectCheckpointsByAge` and `resolveLatestCheckpointFromMap`.** `CollectCheckpointsByAge` returns `[]*CheckpointInfo` (pointer slice), while `resolveLatestCheckpointFromMap` accepts and returns `CheckpointInfo` (value). At line 279, the code does `latest := sorted[len(sorted)-1]` which is a `*CheckpointInfo`, then looks it up again in `infoMap` by `latest.CheckpointID`. This works but is slightly indirect -- the `*CheckpointInfo` from the tree read has all the necessary fields already. This is cosmetic and not a correctness issue.

### Summary

This is a solid, focused fix with good test coverage. The main actionable item is the redundant tree I/O in `resolveLatestCheckpointFromMap` (issue 1), which could be simplified. The rest are minor suggestions. The deduplication of `CollectCheckpointsByAge` is clean, and the overall approach correctly aligns rewind behavior with resume behavior for squash merge commits.

input.command:
cat <<'EOF' | pbcopy
## Fix: `entire rewind` loses checkpoints from squash merge commits

### Problem

When a squash merge commit contains multiple `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers (one per original commit), `entire rewind` only found the first one. `GetLogsOnlyRewindPoints()` used `trailers.ParseCheckpoint()`, which calls `FindStringSubmatch` — returning only the first regex match.

For example, a squash merge of commits A, B, and C would produce a commit message containing three `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers. Only checkpoint A was surfaced in the rewind list; checkpoints B and C were silently inaccessible despite their data existing on `entire/checkpoints/v1`.

### Fix

Switched `GetLogsOnlyRewindPoints()` from `ParseCheckpoint` (single match) to `ParseAllCheckpoints` (all matches). When multiple checkpoint IDs are found in a commit, the new `resolveLatestCheckpointFromMap` helper picks the one with the most recent `CreatedAt` timestamp from the already-loaded checkpoint metadata — no additional tree I/O needed.

This matches how `entire resume` handles squash merges: resolve to the latest checkpoint, show one entry per commit.

### Changes

- **`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_rewind.go`** (+28 lines)
  - `GetLogsOnlyRewindPoints()`: `ParseCheckpoint` → `ParseAllCheckpoints` + resolve to latest
  - New `resolveLatestCheckpointFromMap()` helper

- **`cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/logs_only_rewind_test.go`** (+128 lines)
  - `REDACTED`: creates two sessions with separate checkpoints, simulates a squash merge, verifies the latest checkpoint ID is selected and the correct transcript is restored
EOF

1→# E2E Tests
     2→
     3→End-to-end tests for the `entire` CLI against real agents (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, OpenCode).
     4→
     5→## Commands
     6→
     7→```bash
     8→mise run test:e2e [filter]                          # run filtered (or omit filter for all agents)
     9→mise run test:e2e --agent claude-code [filter]       # Claude Code only
    10→mise run test:e2e --agent gemini-cli [filter]        # Gemini CLI only
    11→mise run test:e2e --agent opencode [filter]          # OpenCode only
    12→go build ./...                                      # compile check (no agent CLI needed)
    13→```
    14→
    15→**Do NOT run E2E tests proactively.** They make real API calls that consume tokens and cost money. Only run when explicitly asked.
    16→
    17→## Structure
    18→
    19→```
    20→e2e/
    21→├── agents/       # Agent abstraction (Agent interface, tmux sessions, concurrency gates)
    22→├── bootstrap/    # CI pre-test setup (auth config, warmup)
    23→├── entire/       # `entire` CLI wrapper (enable, rewind, etc.)
    24→├── exploratory/  # Experimental tests, not run by CI
    25→├── tests/        # Blessed test files (run by CI)
    26→└── testutil/     # Repo setup, assertions, artifact capture
    27→```
    28→
    29→## Key Patterns
    30→
    31→- Every test uses `testutil.ForEachAgent` which runs it per registered agent with repo setup, concurrency gating, and timeout scaling.
    32→- All operations go through `RepoState` (`s.RunPrompt`, `s.Git`) so they're logged to `console.log`.
    33→- Use the `entire` package for CLI interactions, not raw `exec.Command`.
    34→- Skip tests pending CLI fixes with `t.Skip("ENT-XXX: reason")`.
    35→
    36→## Adding a New Agent
    37→
    38→1. Create `agents/<name>.go` implementing the `Agent` interface.
    39→2. Register it in `init()` with `Register(&YourAgent{})`.
    40→3. Add a `Bootstrap()` method for any CI-specific setup (auth config, warmup).
    41→4. Add a `RegisterGate("<name>", N)` call if concurrency needs limiting.
    42→5. Ensure the agent name is accepted by `mise run test:e2e --agent <name>`.
    43→6. Add the agent to `.github/workflows/e2e.yml` matrix and `e2e-isolated.yml` options.
    44→
    45→## Environment Variables
    46→
    47→| Variable | Description | Default |
    48→|----------|-------------|---------|
    49→| `E2E_AGENT` | Agent to test (`claude-code`, `gemini-cli`, `opencode`) | all registered |
    50→| `E2E_ENTIRE_BIN` | Path to a pre-built `entire` binary | builds from source |
    51→| `E2E_TIMEOUT` | Timeout per prompt | `2m` |
    52→| `E2E_KEEP_REPOS` | Set to `1` to preserve temp repos after test | unset |
    53→| `E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR` | Override artifact output directory | `e2e/artifacts/<timestamp>` |
    54→| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Required for Claude Code | — |
    55→| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | Required for Gemini CLI | — |
    56→
    57→## Debugging Failures
    58→
    59→Artifacts are captured to `e2e/artifacts/` on every run (git-log, git-tree, console.log, checkpoint metadata, entire logs). Set `E2E_KEEP_REPOS=1` to preserve the temp repo — a symlink appears in the artifact dir pointing to it.
    60→
    61→Use the `debug-e2e` skill (`.claude/skills/debug-e2e/`) for a structured workflow when investigating failures.
    62→
    63→### Reading artifacts
    64→
    65→- `console.log` — full operation transcript including agent stdout/stderr
    66→- `git-log.txt` — commit history at time of failure
    67→- `git-tree.txt` — working tree state
    68→- `entire-logs/` — internal CLI logs
    69→
    70→### Fixing flaky tests
    71→
    72→When a test passes on retry but failed once, the problem is usually agent non-determinism, not a CLI bug. Common patterns:
    73→
    74→- **Agent asked for confirmation instead of acting**: The model output contains "Does this look right?" or "Should I proceed?". Fix: append "Do not ask for confirmation, just make the change." to the prompt.
    75→- **Agent wrote to wrong path or created extra files**: Fix: be more explicit about exact file paths and what _not_ to do.
    76→- **Agent committed when it shouldn't have**: Fix: add "Do not commit" to the prompt.
    77→- **Checkpoint wait timeout**: `WaitForCheckpoint` or `WaitForCheckpointAdvanceFrom` exceeded deadline. Fix: increase the timeout argument.
    78→
    79→To diagnose: read `console.log` in the failing test's artifact directory. Compare what the agent actually did vs what the test expected.
    80→
    81→## CI Workflows
    82→
    83→- **`.github/workflows/e2e.yml`** — Runs full suite on push to main. Matrix: `[claude, opencode, gemini]`.
    84→- **`.github/workflows/e2e-isolated.yml`** — Manual dispatch for debugging a single test. Inputs: agent + test name filter.
    85→
    86→Both workflows run `go run ./e2e/bootstrap` before tests to handle agent-specific CI setup (auth config, warmup).

    18→// TestRewindPreCommit: agent creates two files in sequence (no user commit),
    19→// then rewinds to the point after the first file was created.
    20→func TestRewindPreCommit(t *testing.T) {
    21→	testutil.ForEachAgent(t, 3*time.Minute, func(t *testing.T, s *testutil.RepoState, ctx context.Context) {
    22→		// Agent creates file A.
    23→		_, err := s.RunPrompt(t, ctx,
    24→			"create a markdown file at docs/red.md with a paragraph about the colour red. Do not ask for confirmation, just make the change.")
    25→		if err != nil {
    26→			t.Fatalf("agent prompt 1 failed: %v", err)
    27→		}
    28→		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "docs/red.md")
    29→
    30→		pointsAfterA := entire.RewindList(t, s.Dir)
    31→		require.NotEmpty(t, pointsAfterA, "expected at least 1 rewind point after file A")
    32→
    33→		// Agent creates file B.
    34→		_, err = s.RunPrompt(t, ctx,
    35→			"create a markdown file at docs/blue.md with a paragraph about the colour blue. Do not ask for confirmation, just make the change.")
    36→		if err != nil {
    37→			t.Fatalf("agent prompt 2 failed: %v", err)
    38→		}
    39→		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "docs/blue.md")
    40→
    41→		pointsAfterB := entire.RewindList(t, s.Dir)
    42→		require.Greater(t, len(pointsAfterB), len(pointsAfterA),
    43→			"expected more rewind points after file B")
    44→
    45→		// Rewind to the first rewind point (after file A was created).
    46→		rewindID := pointsAfterA[0].ID
    47→		err = entire.Rewind(t, s.Dir, rewindID)
    48→		require.NoError(t, err, "rewind to %s should succeed", rewindID)
    49→
    50→		// File A should still exist, file B should be gone.
    51→		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "docs/red.md")
    52→		_, statErr := os.Stat(filepath.Join(s.Dir, "docs", "blue.md"))
    53→		assert.True(t, os.IsNotExist(statErr),
    54→			"docs/blue.md should not exist after rewind, stat error: %v", statErr)
    55→	})
    56→}

    58→// TestRewindAfterCommit: pre-commit shadow branch rewind points should become
    59→// invalid after a user commit. Rewinding to an old shadow branch ID should fail.
    60→func TestRewindAfterCommit(t *testing.T) {
    61→	testutil.ForEachAgent(t, 3*time.Minute, func(t *testing.T, s *testutil.RepoState, ctx context.Context) {
    62→		// Agent creates a file.
    63→		_, err := s.RunPrompt(t, ctx,
    64→			"create a markdown file at docs/red.md with a paragraph about the colour red. Do not commit the file. Do not ask for confirmation, just make the change.")
    65→		if err != nil {
    66→			t.Fatalf("agent failed: %v", err)
    67→		}
    68→		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "docs/red.md")
    69→
    70→		// Get pre-commit rewind points (shadow branch).
    71→		pointsBefore := entire.RewindList(t, s.Dir)
    72→		require.NotEmpty(t, pointsBefore, "expected rewind points before commit")
    73→
    74→		// Find a non-logs-only point (shadow branch ID).
    75→		var shadowPoint *entire.RewindPoint
    76→		for i := range pointsBefore {
    77→			if !pointsBefore[i].IsLogsOnly {
    78→				shadowPoint = &pointsBefore[i]
    79→				break
    80→			}
    81→		}
    82→		require.NotNil(t, shadowPoint, "expected at least one shadow branch rewind point")
    83→		oldID := shadowPoint.ID
    84→
    85→		// User commits the file.
    86→		s.Git(t, "add", ".")
    87→		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "Add red.md")
    88→
    89→		testutil.WaitForCheckpoint(t, s, 15*time.Second)
    90→
    91→		// Get rewind points after commit — old shadow IDs should be gone.
    92→		pointsAfter := entire.RewindList(t, s.Dir)
    93→
    94→		// Verify the old shadow branch ID is no longer listed.
    95→		found := false
    96→		for _, p := range pointsAfter {
    97→			if p.ID == oldID && !p.IsLogsOnly {
    98→				found = true
    99→				break
   100→			}
   101→		}
   102→		assert.False(t, found, "old shadow branch rewind point %s should no longer be listed", oldID)
   103→
   104→		// Attempting to rewind to the old shadow branch ID should fail.
   105→		err = entire.Rewind(t, s.Dir, oldID)
   106→		assert.Error(t, err, "rewind to old shadow branch ID should fail after commit")
   107→
   108→		// Working directory should be unchanged — file still committed.
   109→		testutil.AssertFileExists(t, s.Dir, "docs/red.md")
   110→		testutil.AssertNoShadowBranches(t, s.Dir)
   111→	})
   112→}

    57→// TestResumeSquashMergeMultipleCheckpoints: two agent prompts on a feature
    58→// branch each get their own commit and checkpoint. The feature branch is
    59→// squash-merged to main and `entire resume` should find and restore both
    60→// sessions. Tests both squash merge message formats:
    61→//
    62→//   - GitHub format: trailers appear at the top level in the commit body
    63→//     (e.g. "* Add red doc\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: aaa\n\n* Add blue doc\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: bbb")
    64→//   - git CLI format: `git merge --squash` nests original commit messages
    65→//     (including trailers) indented with 4 spaces inside the squash message
    66→//
    67→// Both formats are tested in a single function to share the expensive agent
    68→// prompts. Main is reset between format tests.
    69→func TestResumeSquashMergeMultipleCheckpoints(t *testing.T) {
    70→	testutil.ForEachAgent(t, 5*time.Minute, func(t *testing.T, s *testutil.RepoState, ctx context.Context) {
    71→		mainBranch := testutil.GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "branch", "--show-current")
    72→
    73→		// Commit files from `entire enable` so main has a clean working tree
    74→		// for branch switching and squash merging.
    75→		s.Git(t, "add", ".")
    76→		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "Enable entire")
    77→
    78→		// Create feature branch with two agent-assisted commits.
    79→		s.Git(t, "checkout", "-b", "feature")
    80→
    81→		_, err := s.RunPrompt(t, ctx,
    82→			"create a file at docs/red.md with a paragraph about the colour red. Do not ask for confirmation, just make the change.")
    83→		if err != nil {
    84→			t.Fatalf("prompt 1 failed: %v", err)
    85→		}
    86→
    87→		s.Git(t, "add", ".")
    88→		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "Add red doc")
    89→		testutil.WaitForCheckpoint(t, s, 15*time.Second)
    90→		cp1Ref := testutil.GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")
    91→
    92→		_, err = s.RunPrompt(t, ctx,
    93→			"create a file at docs/blue.md with a paragraph about the colour blue. Do not ask for confirmation, just make the change.")
    94→		if err != nil {
    95→			t.Fatalf("prompt 2 failed: %v", err)
    96→		}
    97→
    98→		s.Git(t, "add", ".")
    99→		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", "Add blue doc")
   100→		testutil.WaitForCheckpointAdvanceFrom(t, s.Dir, cp1Ref, 15*time.Second)
   101→
   102→		// Record checkpoint IDs from both feature branch commits.
   103→		cpID1 := testutil.GetCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD~1")
   104→		cpID2 := testutil.GetCheckpointTrailer(t, s.Dir, "HEAD")
   105→		require.NotEmpty(t, cpID1, "first commit should have checkpoint trailer")
   106→		require.NotEmpty(t, cpID2, "second commit should have checkpoint trailer")
   107→		require.NotEqual(t, cpID1, cpID2, "checkpoint IDs should be distinct")
   108→
   109→		// Save main HEAD so we can reset between format tests.
   110→		s.Git(t, "checkout", mainBranch)
   111→		mainHead := testutil.GitOutput(t, s.Dir, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
   112→
   113→		// --- Format 1: GitHub squash merge ---
   114→		// GitHub puts each original commit message (including trailers) as
   115→		// top-level bullet points in the squash commit body.
   116→		s.Git(t, "merge", "--squash", "feature")
   117→		githubMsg := fmt.Sprintf(
   118→			"Squash merge feature (#1)\n\n* Add red doc\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: %s\n\n* Add blue doc\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: %s",
   119→			cpID1, cpID2,
   120→		)
   121→		s.Git(t, "commit", "-m", githubMsg)
   122→
   123→		out, err := entire.Resume(s.Dir, mainBranch)
   124→		require.NoError(t, err, "github format: entire resume failed: %s", out)
   125→		assert.Contains(t, out, "Restored 2 sessions",
   126→			"github format: squash merge should restore 2 sessions")
   127→
   128→		// Reset main to before the squash merge for the next format test.
   129→		s.Git(t, "reset", "--hard", mainHead)
   130→
   131→		// --- Format 2: git merge --squash ---
   132→		// The git CLI nests original commit messages (with trailers) indented
   133→		// by 4 spaces inside "Squashed commit of the following:".
   134→		s.Git(t, "merge", "--squash", "feature")
   135→
   136→		// Sanity-check: the auto-generated SQUASH_MSG should contain both trailers.
   137→		squashMsgBytes, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(s.Dir, ".git", "SQUASH_MSG"))
   138→		require.NoError(t, err, "read .git/SQUASH_MSG")
   139→		squashMsgStr := string(squashMsgBytes)
   140→		require.Contains(t, squashMsgStr, cpID1,
   141→			"git SQUASH_MSG should contain first checkpoint ID")
   142→		require.Contains(t, squashMsgStr, cpID2,
   143→			"git SQUASH_MSG should contain second checkpoint ID")
   144→
   145→		// Commit using the git-generated squash message directly (not via -m).
   146→		// GIT_EDITOR=true prevents git from opening an editor while letting
   147→		// it use .git/SQUASH_MSG natively with all hooks running.
   148→		commitCmd := exec.Command("git", "commit")
   149→		commitCmd.Dir = s.Dir
   150→		commitCmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0", "GIT_EDITOR=true")
   151→		commitOut, commitErr := commitCmd.CombinedOutput()
   152→		fmt.Fprintf(s.ConsoleLog, "> git commit (GIT_EDITOR=true)\n%s\n", commitOut)
   153→		require.NoError(t, commitErr, "git commit with squash message failed: %s", commitOut)
   154→
   155→		out, err = entire.Resume(s.Dir, mainBranch)
   156→		require.NoError(t, err, "git-cli format: entire resume failed: %s", out)
   157→		assert.Contains(t, out, "Restored 2 sessions",
   158→			"git-cli format: squash merge should restore 2 sessions")
   159→	})
   160→}
